research.topic: apple-build: Apple build and submission technical requirements as of 2026-10-14 (Xcode/SDK minimums, deployment target, screenshots, app icon, Universal Links, TestFlight, export compliance), checked against Expo SDK 57 / RN 0.86

findings.requirement: Current upload minimum: since April 28, 2026, every build uploaded to App Store Connect must be built with Xcode 26 or later using the iOS 26 SDK (or the matching iPadOS/tvOS/visionOS/watchOS 26 SDK). The user's claim of 'Xcode 26 / SDK 26' is correct.
findings.sourceQuote: SDK minimum requirements — Since April 28, 2026 — Apps uploaded to App Store Connect must be built with Xcode 26 or later using an SDK for iOS 26, iPadOS 26, tvOS 26, visionOS 26, or watchOS 26.
findings.implicationForProject: Build with Xcode 26.x. Expo SDK 57 needs Xcode 26.4+ anyway, so meeting Expo's minimum also meets Apple's. Add a CI release check that fails if the Xcode/SDK major version is below 26.

findings.requirement: Next upload minimum, starting April 2027 (Apple gives the month only): iOS/iPadOS apps must be built with the iOS & iPadOS 27 SDK or later and must target iOS 15 or later. Xcode 27 (27A266a) shipped on September 14, 2026, and Xcode 27.1 RC (27A9275) on October 5, 2026.
findings.sourceQuote: Starting April 2027, apps and games uploaded to App Store Connect need to meet the following minimum requirements. iOS and iPadOS apps must be built with the iOS & iPadOS 27 SDK or later, and target iOS 15 or later
findings.implicationForProject: Xcode 27 is not required today. Plan to move to an Expo SDK and EAS image that build with Xcode 27 before April 2027. Expo's EAS image list already has an Xcode 27.0 image tagged sdk-58. Apple's Sept 9, 2026 news post (https://developer.apple.com/news/?id=k1mtkt1k) confirms the SDK-27 rule.

findings.requirement: Minimum deployment target: since September 9, 2026, iOS and iPadOS apps uploaded to App Store Connect must target iOS 13 or later.
findings.sourceQuote: iOS and iPadOS minimum system requirements — Since September 9, 2026 — iOS and iPadOS apps uploaded to App Store Connect must target iOS 13 or later.
findings.implicationForProject: Expo SDK 57's floor of iOS 16.4 already satisfies both this rule and the April 2027 iOS 15 floor. Do not set ios.deploymentTarget below 16.4. Any value from 16.4 upward is compliant.

findings.requirement: Expo SDK 57 platform table: React Native 0.86, React 19.2.3, Node 22.13.x minimum, Android 7+, compileSdk/targetSdk 36, iOS 16.4+, Xcode 26.4+.
findings.implicationForProject: Confirms the project stack (SDK 57 + RN 0.86). For iOS, use deployment target 16.4 or higher and Xcode 26.4 or later. The latest docs page is SDK 57 ('Reference (v57.0.0)').

findings.requirement: On EAS Build, the iOS image tagged for SDK 57 (also currently 'latest') is macos-tahoe-26.5-xcode-26.6, which ships Xcode 26.6 (17F113). Separate images exist for Xcode 27.0 (tagged sdk-58) and Xcode 27.1 RC.
findings.sourceQuote: macos-tahoe-26.5-xcode-26.6 (latest, sdk-57) ... Xcode 26.6 (17F113)
findings.implicationForProject: Pin ios.image in eas.json to 'sdk-57' or 'macos-tahoe-26.5-xcode-26.6' so builds are reproducible and meet the Xcode 26 rule. Don't switch to Xcode 27 images until Expo confirms SDK 57 supports them.

findings.requirement: Screenshot basics: at least 1 and up to 10 screenshots per device size, in .jpeg/.jpg/.png. Required sets: iPhone needs at least one for 'iPhone with Dynamic Island (medium display)'. iPad needs at least one for the 13-inch display, but only if the app supports iPadOS. Screenshots can't include alpha channels or transparency. Apple's page now names device classes, not 6.9"/6.5". Accepted sizes: Dynamic Island medium display 1206x2622 or 1179x2556. Dynamic Island large display (the 6.9" class) 1320x2868, 1290x2796 or 1260x2736. Face ID large display (the 6.5" class) 1284x2778 or 1242x2688.
findings.sourceQuote: iPhone: At least one screenshot for iPhone with Dynamic Island (medium display). iPad (if your app supports iPadOS): At least one screenshot for iPad 13-inch display. ... Note: Images can't include alpha channels or transparencies.
findings.implicationForProject: Apple's page contradicts itself. The header requires the medium-display set, but the Face ID (large display) card says 'Required if app runs on iPhone and screenshots for iPhone with Dynamic Island (large display) aren't provided'. To be safe, prepare portrait sets at 1206x2622 (medium) and 1320x2868 (large), flattened PNG/JPEG with no alpha, for both the Arabic and English localizations. The user's '6.9"/6.5"' labels are outdated.

findings.requirement: iPad screenshots (13-inch: 2064x2752 or 2048x2732 portrait) are required only if the app runs on iPad natively. In Expo, ios.supportsTablet defaults to false. App Review Guideline 2.4.1 encourages iPad support but does not require it.
findings.sourceQuote: 13" display ... 2064 x 2752 pixels (portrait) ... 2048 x 2732 pixels (portrait) ... Requirement: Required if app runs on iPad
findings.implicationForProject: Decide on ios.supportsTablet deliberately. Leaving it false (the Expo default) avoids the iPad screenshot requirement and iPad layout review. Setting it true means 13-inch iPad screenshots plus iPad-responsive and RTL layouts. Guideline 2.4.1 (https://developer.apple.com/app-store/review/guidelines/) says: 'iPhone apps should run on iPad whenever possible.'

findings.requirement: iPhone Duo (on sale October 23, 2026) has screenshot sizes of 1398x2034 for the outer display and 2007x2853 for the inner display. Apple says iPhone Duo screenshots become required in April 2027, but its two statements describe the trigger differently.
findings.sourceQuote: Starting April 2027, any apps or games submitted will need to include screenshots for iPhone Duo. (Screenshot spec page: 'Starting in April 2027, screenshots will be required for any app using the iOS 27.1 SDK or later.')
findings.implicationForProject: Not needed for a 2026 launch on Xcode 26. Add a backlog item to make Duo-responsive layouts and Duo screenshots alongside the Xcode 27 / iOS 27 SDK migration before April 2027.

findings.requirement: App Review Guideline 2.3.3: screenshots must mostly show the app in use. Review approves only submissions where more than half of each device's screenshots show the app in use. Screens that only show login or splash are not acceptable.
findings.sourceQuote: App Review ... will approve only those submissions where more than half of screenshots show the app in use.
findings.implicationForProject: Most screenshots should show real Patient/Doctor/Nurse flows (wound tracking, booking, TetraSol store, AI assistant). Use synthetic, non-identifiable patient data and wound images. Marketing frames must stay a minority.

findings.requirement: App icon spec: on iOS/iPadOS the icon is a square 1024x1024 px layered design. The system masks it to a rounded rectangle and supports default, dark, clear and tinted appearances. Xcode can generate every size from one 1024x1024 image, or icons can be authored in Icon Composer. Any imported background layer must be full-bleed and opaque.
findings.sourceQuote: iOS, iPadOS, macOS | Square | Rounded rectangle (square) | 1024x1024 px | Layered | Default, dark, clear light, clear dark, tinted light, tinted dark ... If you do import a background layer, make sure it's full-bleed and opaque.
findings.implicationForProject: Supply a square 1024x1024 sRGB/P3 master with no pre-rounded corners. Expo's ios.icon accepts a PNG path, a {light, dark, tinted} object, or an Icon Composer '.icon' directory, and says to 'Use a 1024x1024 icon which follows Apple's interface guidelines for icons, including color profile and transparency' (https://docs.expo.dev/versions/latest/config/app/).

findings.requirement: The rule that the 1024x1024 App Store icon must have no alpha channel is enforced at upload (error ITMS-90717 'Invalid large app icon'). It is documented only by developer reports, not on any Apple page fetched today.
findings.sourceQuote: (Developer Forums / third-party reports) ITMS-90717 Invalid large app icon ... can't be transparent or contain an alpha channel
findings.implicationForProject: Flatten the light/default iOS icon PNG onto the brand background with no alpha before building, and add a CI check (e.g. `sips -g hasAlpha` or ImageMagick) that fails if it has alpha. The only exception: Apple's Xcode doc says the dark variant should have a transparent background.

findings.requirement: Universal Links basics: (1) Host a file named exactly 'apple-app-site-association' (no extension) at https://<fully qualified domain>/.well-known/apple-app-site-association. (2) Serve it over HTTPS with a valid certificate and no redirects. (3) Each subdomain needs its own file and its own entitlement entry. (4) Entitlement format is <service>:<fully qualified domain>, e.g. applinks:example.com. (5) appIDs use the form <TeamID>.<BundleID>. (6) Since iOS 14, devices fetch the file through Apple's CDN, which requests it within 24 hours; devices recheck about weekly.
findings.sourceQuote: You must host the file using https:// with a valid certificate and with no redirects. ... Apple's content delivery network requests the apple-app-site-association file for your domain within 24 hours.
findings.implicationForProject: Set ios.associatedDomains, e.g. ['applinks:<domain>'] (no https:// prefix), with one entry per subdomain and per bundle-ID variant (dev/staging/prod). Use Apple's current 'appIDs' + 'components' AASA format; Expo's docs example still uses the older 'appID'/'paths' keys. Paymob payment-return URLs need their own explicit, excluded or included path rules.

findings.requirement: Apple warns that Universal Links are an attack vector. Apps must validate every URL parameter, discard malformed URLs, and must not let a link directly delete content or expose sensitive user information.
findings.sourceQuote: Universal links offer a potential attack vector into your app, so make sure to validate all URL parameters and discard any malformed URLs. In addition, limit the available actions to those that don't risk the user's data.
findings.implicationForProject: Deep links to wound records, consultations, orders or Paymob results must be schema-validated in Expo Router, must require authentication and a role check (patient/doctor/nurse) before showing PHI, and must never trigger destructive or payment actions on their own.

findings.requirement: TestFlight basics: up to 100 internal testers and 10,000 external testers. A build is testable for up to 90 days. Adding the first build to an external group sends it to TestFlight App Review, which approves before testing starts. An internal group must exist before an external group can be created. Up to six builds can go to TestFlight review in 24 hours, with one build per version in review at a time. A Beta App Description and Feedback Email are required for external testing.
findings.sourceQuote: To create an external group for external testing, you must first create an internal group for internal testing. ... You can submit up to six builds for TestFlight App Review within a 24-hour period.
findings.implicationForProject: Release runbook: upload, then internal group (team), then external groups (e.g. pilot doctors/nurses). Provide the Beta App Description (required field per /provide-test-information) and a feedback email, plus 'What to Test' notes. Keep production Paymob keys out of TestFlight builds, or flag them clearly.

findings.requirement: Beta App Review details: contact name, email and phone; a demoAccountRequired flag with demo username and password; notes up to 4,000 characters. The API docs say: 'Credentials must be valid and active for duration of review.' For App Store review, the demo account 'must not expire', and the contact phone must be in international format with '+' (App Store Connect help, reference/app-review-information).
findings.sourceQuote: demoAccountRequired: A Boolean value that indicates if sign-in information is required to review all the features of your app. ... Credentials must be valid and active for duration of review.
findings.implicationForProject: Create permanent review accounts for Patient, Doctor and Nurse, pre-verified and not blocked by OTP or license checks. Put the extra roles' credentials in Notes with clear steps. Use an Egyptian contact phone in +20 format. Keep backend and Paymob sandbox live during review.

findings.requirement: Export compliance: setting ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption=NO in Info.plist declares no encryption or only exempt encryption (Apple gives OS-provided HTTPS via URLSession as typically exempt). YES means non-exempt encryption and usually needs ITSEncryptionExportComplianceCode from Apple's documentation review. Without the key, App Store Connect asks the questionnaire on every upload, and TestFlight builds show 'Missing Compliance' until it is answered. Apps using exempt encryption may still have to file a year-end self-classification report with the US government.
findings.sourceQuote: Set the value to NO if your app—including any third-party libraries it links against—doesn't use encryption, or if it only uses forms of encryption that are exempt from export compliance documentation requirements. Otherwise, set it to YES.
findings.implicationForProject: In Expo, set ios.config.usesNonExemptEncryption (it writes ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption). If the app only uses HTTPS/TLS and OS crypto (Keychain via expo-secure-store, platform crypto), false is likely correct, but the developer is legally responsible for the call. Add any custom or E2E crypto library (e.g. for chat or records) to the review first. Also see https://developer.apple.com/documentation/bundleresources/information-property-list/itsappusesnonexemptencryption.

findings.requirement: Regulated medical device declaration: apps available in the EU/EEA, UK or US must declare whether they are regulated medical devices in App Store Connect if either (a) their primary or secondary category is Health & Fitness or Medical, or (b) they answered 'frequent' to Medical or Treatment Information in the age rating questionnaire. Declaring 'Yes' requires an SRN or FDA number, an instructions-for-use URL, a use statement and safety information.
findings.sourceQuote: apps that are available in the European Union (EU)/European Economic Area (EEA), United Kingdom (UK), or United States (US), and that also meet either of the criteria listed below must indicate whether they're regulated medical device
findings.implicationForProject: If distribution is Egypt-only, this section does not apply as written. If the Medical/Health category is used and the app is also offered in EU/UK/US, answer it, most likely 'No' unless the AI wound features amount to diagnosis or treatment needing CE/UKCA/FDA authorization. Keep store availability limited to Egypt until this is decided.

findings.requirement: Privacy-manifest gate on upload: since May 1, 2024, new or updated apps must include approved reasons for the listed 'required reason' APIs, including APIs used by third-party SDKs.
findings.sourceQuote: You'll need to include approved reasons for the listed APIs used by your app's code (including from third-party SDKs) to upload a new or updated app to App Store Connect.
findings.implicationForProject: Check that the generated PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy covers app code plus all native modules (Expo modules, Paymob SDK, analytics/crash SDKs). Add any missing reasons via ios.privacyManifests in app.config.ts.

findings.requirement: Age rating questionnaire: updated questions were due by January 31, 2026, to avoid blocked submissions. Questions about social media capabilities were added on July 9, 2026, and answers are required for new submissions and updates from September 2026.
findings.sourceQuote: As previously shared, beginning in September 2026, responses will be required when submitting new apps or updates to the App Store
findings.implicationForProject: Complete the full questionnaire, including Medical/Treatment Information and social-media capability. Doctor/patient messaging is likely not a social feed, but answer deliberately. Note that 'frequent' medical information triggers the medical-device declaration for EU/UK/US storefronts.

findings.requirement: An updated Apple Developer Program License Agreement was published on October 13, 2026, and the account holder needs to sign in and accept it.
findings.sourceQuote: The Apple Developer Program License Agreement has been revised ... sign in to your account to accept the updated terms.
findings.implicationForProject: The account holder should accept the new agreement in the developer account before the first upload or submission. The news post does not say whether uploads are blocked until accepted; it only asks for acceptance.

unresolved: Whether Expo SDK 57 officially supports building with Xcode 27 / iOS 27 SDK, which is needed from April 2027. EAS lists the Xcode 27.0 image under 'sdk-58' and keeps 'sdk-57' on Xcode 26.6, so an SDK upgrade may be needed before April 2027.
The exact day in April 2027 when the iOS 27 SDK rule and the 'target iOS 15 or later' rule take effect. Apple gives only 'April 2027'.

Apple's screenshot page contradicts itself: the header requires 'iPhone with Dynamic Island (medium display)', while the Face ID (large display) card refers to Dynamic Island (large display) as the fallback requirement. Uploading both medium and large sets avoids the risk.
What triggers the iPhone Duo screenshot requirement in April 2027: the spec page says apps using the iOS 27.1 SDK or later; the Oct 5, 2026 news post says any apps or games submitted.
No current official Apple page fetched today states that the 1024x1024 App Store icon must have no alpha channel. Only community and third-party reports of upload error ITMS-90717 support it.
Egyptian import or NTRA rules on encryption in apps were not checked. Apple's page mentions only US EAR and French ANSSI controls.
Whether 'Declare Regulated Medical Device Status' will be extended to Egypt or other non-EU/UK/US storefronts. Apple currently lists only EU/EEA, UK and US.

The App Store Connect help link for 'TestFlight App Review information properties' (reference/app-review-information) now leads to the general Platform version information page, so the TestFlight demo-account fields were checked through the App Store Connect API BetaAppReviewDetail docs instead.

research.topic: apple-privacy: App Privacy labels, PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy / Required Reason APIs, third-party SDK manifests and signatures, Guideline 5.1.1 (account deletion, permissions, purpose strings), 4.8 Login Services / Sign in with Apple, ATT. Verified 2026-10-14. The App Review Guidelines page reads "Last Updated: June 8, 2026".

findings.requirement: The App Review Guidelines in force today were last updated on June 8, 2026. Every guideline quote below comes from that version.
findings.sourceQuote: Last Updated: June 8, 2026
findings.implicationForProject: Cite this version in the compliance docs. Check the guidelines again before each submission.

findings.requirement: Guideline 4.8 applies only when a third-party or social login (Facebook, Google, X, LinkedIn, Amazon, WeChat and similar) sets up or authenticates the user's primary account. In that case the app must also offer an equivalent login service that limits data collection to name and email, lets the user keep their email private, and does not collect interactions for advertising without consent. No other login service is needed when the app uses only the company's own account system. Since the 2024 rewording, the guideline no longer names Sign in with Apple specifically.
findings.sourceQuote: Another login service is not required if: Your app exclusively uses your company's own account setup and sign-in systems.
findings.implicationForProject: Sign in with Apple is NOT required. The app only uses its own email/password and phone OTP, both through Better Auth, its own backend. Do not add the expo-apple-authentication plugin or the entitlement. If Google, Facebook or any other social login is added later for any role, 4.8 starts to apply, and Sign in with Apple becomes the practical way to comply. Keep a regression check on this.

findings.requirement: Guideline 5.1.1(v): an app that supports account creation must let users delete their account from inside the app. An app without significant account-based features must work without a login. Apps may not require personal information unless it is directly relevant to the core functionality or required by law. Apple's news post set the enforcement date as June 30, 2022.
findings.sourceQuote: If your app supports account creation, you must also offer account deletion within the app.
findings.implicationForProject: All three roles (Patient, Doctor, Nurse) need an easy-to-find in-app 'Delete account' entry under Account/Settings. It must delete the account, not just deactivate it. Personal data should be requested only where it is needed. Consider letting guests browse public content, such as the TetraSol catalog or education pages, without logging in. This is recommended, not mandatory, because the app has significant account-based features.

findings.requirement: Apple's account-deletion support page sets these rules. The option must be easy to find, typically in account settings. The app must offer to delete the entire account record and associated personal data; deactivation alone is insufficient. A link straight to a web deletion page is allowed. Apps in highly regulated industries under 5.1.1(ix) may add customer-service flows to confirm deletion, while other apps must not require calls, emails or chat. A confirmation step is fine. Manual deletion that takes time is acceptable if the user is told how long it will take and gets a confirmation when it is done. Users with an auto-renewable subscription must be told that billing continues through Apple. Deletion can be scheduled for the subscription's expiry only if an immediate-deletion option also exists.
findings.sourceQuote: Offer to delete the entire account record, along with associated personal data. You may include additional options, but only offering to temporarily deactivate or disable an account is insufficient.
findings.implicationForProject: Build an in-app deletion flow: confirmation, a stated timeline, then a completion notice. As healthcare, the app may add a verification or customer-service step, but it must not make deletion unnecessarily hard. Where Egyptian law requires keeping medical or transaction records, document what is retained and why; local law was not verified here. If Silver/Gold/Platinum are sold as auto-renewable IAP subscriptions, the deletion flow must warn that Apple billing continues and tell the user to cancel. Sign in with Apple token revocation does not apply because Sign in with Apple is not used.

findings.requirement: Guideline 5.1.1(i): every app must link its privacy policy both in the App Store Connect metadata field and inside the app, in an easily accessible place. The policy must say what data is collected, how, and all of its uses. It must confirm that third parties (analytics, SDKs and others) give equal protection. It must explain retention and deletion and how to revoke consent or request deletion.
findings.sourceQuote: All apps must include a link to their privacy policy in the App Store Connect metadata field and within the app in an easily accessible manner.
findings.implicationForProject: Publish Arabic and English privacy policies covering wound photos and health data, AI assistant processing, Paymob payments, doctor and nurse matching, retention and deletion. Link the policy in App Store Connect and from a Privacy Center screen in the app.

findings.requirement: Guidelines 5.1.1(ii) to (iv), on permission, data minimization and access. Apps must get consent before collecting user or usage data. Paid functionality must not depend on granting data access. Users need an easy way to withdraw consent. Purpose strings must clearly and completely describe the use. Apps should request only data relevant to core functionality, preferring out-of-process pickers over full Photos or Contacts access. Apps must not manipulate or force consent to unnecessary access, and should offer alternatives, such as manual address entry when Location is declined.
findings.sourceQuote: Paid functionality must not be dependent on or require a user to grant access to this data. ... Ensure your purpose strings clearly and completely describe your use of the data.
findings.implicationForProject: Request camera and photos only at the moment a wound photo is taken. Prefer the system photo picker (PHPicker, as used by expo-image-picker) over full library access. Request location only for nurse or home-visit matching, and offer manual address entry when it is declined. Silver/Gold/Platinum benefits must not depend on granting location, notifications or tracking. Do not add permissions for features that are not shipped, such as microphone or contacts.

findings.requirement: Purpose-string rules from Apple's 'Requesting access to protected resources' page. A string must not be blank. It must be under 4,000 bytes. It must accurately and specifically explain why access is needed, and these rules apply to localized strings too. App Review rejects binaries whose code references a protected API without the matching key (ITMS-90683). Accessing a resource without the string fails and may crash the app. Localize each string for every locale the app supports.
findings.sourceQuote: App Review checks for the use of protected resources, and rejects apps that contain code accessing those resources without a purpose string.
findings.implicationForProject: Set specific Arabic and English strings (NSCameraUsageDescription, NSPhotoLibraryUsageDescription and NSLocationWhenInUseUsageDescription if used) through the Expo plugin options or ios.infoPlist. Add Arabic translations through the Expo 'locales' map ({"ar": "./languages/ar.json"} with an ios.NS*UsageDescription key in each file). The current apps/mobile/app.json already sets CFBundleAllowMixedLocalizations=true, as Expo requires. Remove permission plugins for unused features so their API references and keys do not ship.

findings.requirement: Expo localizes iOS permission messages per locale. Set ios.infoPlist.CFBundleAllowMixedLocalizations: true and point 'locales' at JSON files whose 'ios' object holds the usage-description keys. Prebuild writes these values into each locale's InfoPlist.strings.
findings.sourceQuote: To show a translated system permission message, add the matching usage-description key to the ios object in each locale file. During prebuild, Expo writes those values to InfoPlist.strings for the corresponding locale.
findings.implicationForProject: Add apps/mobile/languages/ar.json and en.json with CFBundleDisplayName ('غير لي' / 'Dress My Wound') and every NS*UsageDescription key. Register them under expo.locales.

findings.requirement: Guideline 5.1.1(ix): apps that provide services in highly regulated fields, including healthcare, should be submitted by a legal entity that provides the services, not by an individual developer.
findings.sourceQuote: Apps that provide services in highly regulated fields (such as banking and financial services, healthcare, ...) ... should be submitted by a legal entity that provides the services, and not by an individual developer.
findings.implicationForProject: Enroll in the Apple Developer Program as an organization, the Egyptian company that provides or contracts the healthcare services. An individual account is likely to be rejected. The seller name shown should match that entity.

findings.requirement: Guideline 5.1.2(i), current text: personal data may not be used, sent or shared without permission. Sharing with third parties, explicitly including third-party AI, must be clearly disclosed and explicitly permitted first. Tracking requires App Tracking Transparency permission. Apps may not require users to enable push, location or tracking to access functionality or receive compensation.
findings.effectiveDate: Text present in the June 8, 2026 version. Secondary sources say the AI wording was added on Nov 13, 2025.
findings.sourceQuote: You must clearly disclose where personal data will be shared with third parties, including with third-party AI, and obtain explicit permission before doing so.
findings.implicationForProject: If the AI assistant sends user messages, wound photos or health data to an external model provider, show a clear disclosure naming the provider type and data and get an explicit opt-in before first use, with a way to withdraw. Without consent, AI features must stay off. Subscription tiers must not require enabling push notifications or location.

findings.requirement: Guideline 5.1.3 on health data. Health, fitness and medical data may not be used or disclosed for advertising, marketing or data mining, except to improve health management or for health research, and then only with permission. The specific health data collected from the device must be disclosed. Apps may not store personal health information in iCloud. Guideline 5.1.2(vi) bars using Camera or Photo API depth and facial-mapping data for marketing.
findings.sourceQuote: Apps must not write false or inaccurate data into HealthKit or any other medical research or health management apps, and may not store personal health information in iCloud.
findings.implicationForProject: Do not use CloudKit, iCloud Drive or NSUbiquitous storage for wound photos or records; keep them on the backend. Never use health data for marketing, including TetraSol product promotions, without separate permission. Whether ordinary iCloud device backups count as 'storing in iCloud' is not stated, so consider marking cached PHI files isExcludedFromBackup and keeping them in SecureStore or encrypted storage.

findings.requirement: Guideline 1.4.1: medical apps that could give inaccurate data, or be used to diagnose or treat patients, may get greater review scrutiny. Apps must disclose data and methodology behind accuracy claims and should remind users to check with a doctor before making medical decisions. If the app has regulatory clearance, a link to it should be submitted.
findings.sourceQuote: Apps should remind users to check with a doctor in addition to using the app and before making medical decisions.
findings.implicationForProject: Show 'consult a doctor' disclaimers on AI assistant answers and on wound guidance, plus emergency guidance. Make no diagnostic accuracy claims. Prepare App Review notes explaining the clinician roles and how they are verified.

findings.requirement: The privacy manifest is a file named PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy at the root of the iOS app bundle. Its top-level keys are NSPrivacyTracking (Boolean), NSPrivacyTrackingDomains (required when tracking is true), NSPrivacyCollectedDataTypes and NSPrivacyAccessedAPITypes. Every privacy manifest in the app must be valid, and App Store Connect rejects submissions containing invalid ones. TN3181 says that since November 12, 2024 a valid manifest has been required (error ITMS-91056 for invalid files).
findings.sourceQuote: App Store Connect rejects app submissions that include invalid privacy manifest files.
findings.implicationForProject: Ship an app-level manifest with NSPrivacyTracking=false and no tracking domains. Declare NSPrivacyCollectedDataTypes for what the app collects (see the data-types finding) and NSPrivacyAccessedAPITypes. Do not invent keys or values, because Xcode's privacy report breaks on custom values.

findings.requirement: Required Reason API declarations have been mandatory since May 1, 2024. App Store Connect does not accept apps that use a required reason API without an approved reason in the privacy manifest. Each executable or dynamic library bundle needs its own manifest. An SDK cannot rely on the app's manifest, and declared reasons must match the app's real functionality and must not be used for tracking. Fingerprinting is not allowed, regardless of ATT permission.
findings.sourceQuote: Starting May 1, 2024, apps that don't describe their use of required reason API in their privacy manifest file aren't accepted by App Store Connect.
findings.implicationForProject: Declare reasons for every required reason API used by app code and by statically linked pods. React Native 0.86 aggregation, described below, covers most pods automatically. Check the merged manifest in the prebuilt ios/ project before upload.

findings.requirement: NSPrivacyAccessedAPICategoryUserDefaults (UserDefaults) has four reasons. CA92.1: read and write information accessible only to the app itself. 1C8F.1: data shared within the same App Group. C56D.1: a third-party SDK wrapper used only when the app calls it. AC6B.1: the MDM managed-configuration or feedback keys.
findings.sourceQuote: CA92.1 => Declare this reason to access user defaults to read and write information that is only accessible to the app itself.
findings.implicationForProject: Declare UserDefaults with CA92.1. React Native core and expo-constants declare it, and so does the RN template. Add 1C8F.1 only if an App Group is added later, for example for a widget or notification extension.

findings.requirement: NSPrivacyAccessedAPICategoryFileTimestamp (creationDate, modificationDate, stat/fstat/lstat, getattrlist and related APIs) has four reasons. DDA9.1: display timestamps to the user, with no off-device use. C617.1: metadata of files inside the app container, app group container or the app's CloudKit container. 3B52.1: files the user explicitly granted access to, for example through a document picker. 0A2A.1: third-party SDK wrappers only.
findings.sourceQuote: C617.1 => Declare this reason to access the timestamps, size, or other metadata of files inside the app container, app group container, or the app's CloudKit container.
findings.implicationForProject: Declare FileTimestamp with C617.1; RN core declares it too. Add 3B52.1 only if wound documents are imported through a document picker and their metadata is read. A note for anyone reusing memory-based lists: 3B52.1, not 0A2A.1, is the reason for user-granted files.

findings.requirement: NSPrivacyAccessedAPICategorySystemBootTime (systemUptime, mach_absolute_time()) has three reasons. 35F9.1: measure time elapsed between in-app events or run timers; elapsed time may be sent off-device. 8FFB.1: calculate absolute timestamps for in-app events. 3D61.1: an optional bug report the user chooses to submit.
findings.sourceQuote: 35F9.1 => Declare this reason to access the system boot time in order to measure the amount of time that has elapsed between events that occurred within the app or to perform calculations to enable timers.
findings.implicationForProject: Declare SystemBootTime with 35F9.1. React Native core and the RN template use it.

findings.requirement: NSPrivacyAccessedAPICategoryDiskSpace (volumeAvailableCapacity*Key, volumeTotalCapacityKey, systemFreeSize, systemSize, statfs/statvfs and related APIs) has four reasons. 85F4.1: display disk space to the user. E174.1: check whether there is enough space to write files, or delete files when space is low, with user-observable behavior. 7D9E.1: an optional user-submitted bug report. B728.1: health research apps only. ActiveKeyboards has two reasons: 3EC4.1 for custom keyboard apps and 54BD.1 for customizing UI based on active keyboards.
findings.sourceQuote: E174.1 => Declare this reason to check whether there is sufficient disk space to write files, or to check whether the disk space is low so that the app can delete files when the disk space is low.
findings.implicationForProject: Declare DiskSpace (usually E174.1) only if a dependency such as expo-file-system, expo-updates or an image cache, or app code, actually calls these APIs. Rely on each pod's manifest plus aggregation. Do not declare B728.1, because Dress My Wound is not solely a health-research app. ActiveKeyboards is likely not needed.

findings.requirement: Apple lists 86 commonly used third-party SDKs that need their own privacy manifest. This applies when a new app includes them or an update adds them, and a signature is also required when the SDK is a binary dependency. Any version, and any SDK that repackages a listed one, is covered. Apple's docs say this has been enforced since February 12, 2025 (warning email ITMS-91061). The list includes hermes, FirebaseAuth/Core/Messaging/Crashlytics/Installations, GoogleSignIn, OneSignal, SDWebImage, Lottie, FBSDK*, AppAuth, GTMAppAuth, Alamofire and others.
findings.sourceQuote: You must include the privacy manifest for any SDK listed below when you submit new apps in App Store Connect that include those SDKs ... Signatures are also required in these cases where the listed SDKs are used as binary dependencies.
findings.implicationForProject: The first submission is a 'new app', so every listed SDK in the build must ship a valid manifest. That includes hermes (React Native's JS engine, a prebuilt binary) and SDWebImage (pulled in by expo-image, if used). If Firebase or OneSignal is added for OTP or push, use current versions that include manifests and signatures. Watch for ITMS-91061 or invalid-signature emails after the first TestFlight upload.

findings.requirement: React Native 0.86 merges privacy manifests automatically at pod install. use_react_native! defaults to privacy_file_aggregation_enabled: true and gathers the NSPrivacyAccessedAPITypes reasons from every pod, plus React Native core's own (FileTimestamp C617.1, UserDefaults CA92.1, SystemBootTime 35F9.1), into the app target's PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy. The Expo SDK 57 bare template (expo ~57.0.28, react-native 0.86.3) passes privacy_file_aggregation_enabled unless Podfile.properties sets 'apple.privacyManifestAggregationEnabled' to 'false'. Only accessed-API reasons are merged, not collected data types.
findings.sourceQuote: # Get all required reason APIs defined in current pods ... # Add the Required Reason APIs from React Native core
findings.implicationForProject: Leave aggregation on; do not set apple.privacyManifestAggregationEnabled=false. NSPrivacyCollectedDataTypes and NSPrivacyTracking still have to be written by us, through ios.privacyManifests. Expo template Podfile: https://github.com/expo/expo/blob/sdk-57/templates/expo-template-bare-minimum/ios/Podfile.

findings.requirement: In Expo SDK 57, the app config field ios.privacyManifests (with NSPrivacyAccessedAPITypes, NSPrivacyTracking, NSPrivacyTrackingDomains and NSPrivacyCollectedDataTypes[{NSPrivacyCollectedDataType, ...Linked, ...Tracking, ...Purposes}]) is written into the native PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy at prebuild. Expo SDK packages that use required reason APIs include their own PrivacyInfo file. Expo warns that Apple does not correctly parse all PrivacyInfo files from static CocoaPods dependencies, so reasons may also need adding at app level. A third-party library's reasons can be found in node_modules/<pkg>/ios/PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy.
findings.sourceQuote: Apple does not correctly parse all the PrivacyInfo files included by static CocoaPods dependencies, you may need to add the required reasons to your app's PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy file or to app.json
findings.implicationForProject: apps/mobile/app.json currently has NO ios.privacyManifests block. Add one (in the planned app.config.ts) with NSPrivacyTracking:false, NSPrivacyAccessedAPITypes [UserDefaults CA92.1, FileTimestamp C617.1, SystemBootTime 35F9.1, plus DiskSpace E174.1 if any dependency uses it], and NSPrivacyCollectedDataTypes matching the nutrition label. Config reference: https://docs.expo.dev/versions/v57.0.0/config/app/ (ios.privacyManifests).

findings.requirement: Collected data types for the manifest and the nutrition label use fixed keys. Relevant ones include NSPrivacyCollectedDataTypeHealth, PhotosorVideos, Name, EmailAddress, PhoneNumber, PhysicalAddress, PreciseLocation, CoarseLocation, PaymentInfo, PurchaseHistory, UserID, DeviceID, CustomerSupport, OtherUserContent, AudioData, ProductInteraction, CrashData, PerformanceData and SensitiveInfo. The purpose keys are ThirdPartyAdvertising, DeveloperAdvertising, Analytics, ProductPersonalization, AppFunctionality and Other. The app's manifest does not need to cover data that third-party SDKs collect, since SDKs ship their own. Xcode's Product > Archive > Generate Privacy Report combines all manifests for filling in App Store Connect.
findings.sourceQuote: Xcode won't generate a privacy report correctly if you define your own collected data types for the NSPrivacyCollectedDataType key, or provide your own reasons for the NSPrivacyCollectedDataTypePurposes key.
findings.implicationForProject: Expected declarations, each Linked=true, Tracking=false, purpose AppFunctionality: Health (wound records), PhotosorVideos (wound photos), Name, EmailAddress, PhoneNumber, PhysicalAddress (deliveries and home visits), PurchaseHistory, UserID, CustomerSupport, OtherUserContent (AI chat, messages), and Precise or Coarse Location if used. Add Analytics or crash purposes only if analytics or crash SDKs are added. Generate the Xcode privacy report from an archive and reconcile it with App Store Connect.

findings.requirement: App Privacy details (the nutrition label) are required to submit new apps and updates. They cover the developer's own practices and those of integrated third-party code. 'Collect' means sending data off-device so it can be accessed longer than needed to serve the request in real time. Data is optional to disclose only if ALL the optional-disclosure criteria are met. Payment Info need not be disclosed if a payment service collects it outside the app and the developer never has access. Each data type needs a linked-to-user flag, a tracking flag and its purposes. Answers must be kept accurate and can be updated without an app update.
findings.sourceQuote: If your app uses a payment service, the payment information is entered outside your app, and you as the developer never have access to the payment information, it is not collected and does not need to be disclosed.
findings.implicationForProject: In App Store Connect, declare Health, Photos or Videos, Contact Info, User ID, Purchase History, Customer Support, Other User Content and Location (if used) as Data Linked to You for App Functionality; declare nothing under 'Used to Track You'. Card data entered only in Paymob's hosted checkout or SDK can be left out of Payment Info only if the backend never receives it. Still review Paymob SDK data collection, since third-party SDK practices must be included. Update the label whenever an SDK or AI provider changes.

findings.requirement: ATT and tracking. Tracking means linking app data with other companies' data for targeted advertising or ad measurement, or sharing data with data brokers. Tracking or reading the IDFA requires permission through the AppTrackingTransparency framework, which needs NSUserTrackingUsageDescription (the app crashes without it). Apps may not gate features on, or reward, tracking consent (5.1.2(i)). Using IDFV for analytics across the same developer's apps does not need ATT. Deriving data to uniquely identify a device (fingerprinting) is prohibited, and SDKs that do so can cause rejection.
findings.sourceQuote: Your app needs to use the App Tracking Transparency framework if it collects data about people and shares it with other companies to track them across apps and websites.
findings.implicationForProject: The app has no ad or attribution SDKs and does no cross-company tracking, so ATT is not needed. Do NOT add expo-tracking-transparency, NSUserTrackingUsageDescription or an ATT prompt. Set NSPrivacyTracking=false. If marketing later adds Meta, AppsFlyer, Adjust or a similar attribution SDK, ATT, tracking domains and label changes become mandatory. Never tie subscription perks to tracking consent. ATT framework docs: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/apptrackingtransparency

findings.requirement: Apple's Upcoming Requirements page, for context. Since April 28, 2026, uploads must be built with Xcode 26 or later using an iOS 26 SDK. Since September 9, 2026, iOS and iPadOS apps must target iOS 13 or later. Approved-reason declarations are listed as required since May 1, 2024.
findings.sourceQuote: Apps uploaded to App Store Connect must be built with Xcode 26 or later using an SDK for iOS 26
findings.implicationForProject: Build on EAS with an Xcode 26+ image; Expo SDK 57 defaults should comply, but confirm the eas.json image. This is not a privacy item, but it blocks upload if missed.

unresolved: Hermes is on Apple's list of SDKs that need a privacy manifest and signature, and React Native ships it as a prebuilt binary. Searching the RN 0.86-stable hermes-engine.podspec for 'privacy' or signing terms found nothing, so it is unconfirmed whether the hermes xcframework in RN 0.86.3 / Expo SDK 57 carries a valid manifest and signature. Check this on the first TestFlight upload (look for ITMS-91061 or signature emails).
The date Apple added 'including with third-party AI' to 5.1.2(i) comes only from secondary sources (Nov 13, 2025). The current text itself is verified in the June 8, 2026 guidelines.

Guideline 5.1.3(ii) bars storing personal health information in iCloud, but Apple does not say whether standard iCloud device backups of the app container count. Treat it as a conservative implementation choice to exclude PHI caches from backup.

Apple's wording varies on whether the listed-SDK requirement applies to every app update or only updates that add a listed SDK (the SDK page vs. the ITMS-91061 email). It does not matter for the first submission, which is a 'new app'.

Whether Paymob's iOS SDK or hosted checkout ships a PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy, and what data it collects, was not checked. Paymob is not on Apple's list. This must be reviewed before filling in the nutrition label.

Egyptian legal retention periods for medical and transaction records were not checked. They affect how far 'delete the entire account record' can go in practice and what retention disclosures are needed.

The installed dependency tree (node_modules not installed in the repo) was not inspected for the exact required reason API categories, such as DiskSpace. The final manifest must be generated by expo prebuild plus pod install and then reviewed.
Whether App Review penalizes an ATT prompt in an app that does not track was not verified. Moot if ATT is simply left out, as recommended.

research.topic: apple-health-payments: Apple App Review Guidelines on health/medical apps, payments (IAP vs. Paymob), subscriptions, external purchase links for the Egypt storefront, and organization-account requirements. Guidelines page shows 'Last Updated: June 8, 2026' (verified 2026-10-14).

findings.requirement: The App Review Guidelines page currently in force shows 'Last Updated: June 8, 2026'. That revision changed the Introduction (kid and teen safety), 1.2, 4.3(a), 4.3(b) and 4.5.3. It did not change 1.4.1, 3.1.x or 5.1.x.
findings.sourceQuote: Introduction: revised kid and teen safety guidance. 1.2: new paragraph... 4.3(a)... 4.3(b)... 4.5.3: clarifies that Live Activities may not be used to spam, phish...
findings.implicationForProject: Use the June 8, 2026 text as the compliance baseline. The health and payment clauses quoted below are current.

findings.requirement: 1.4.1: Medical apps that could give inaccurate information, or that could be used to diagnose or treat patients, get greater scrutiny. They must disclose data and methodology for any health-measurement accuracy claims, and are rejected if accuracy cannot be validated. They should remind users to check with a doctor. If the app has regulatory clearance, a link to that documentation must be submitted.
findings.sourceQuote: Medical apps that could provide inaccurate data or information, or that could be used for diagnosing or treating patients may be reviewed with greater scrutiny... Apps should remind users to check with a doctor in addition to using the app and before making medical decisions.If your medical app has received regulatory clearance, please submit a link to that documentation with your app.
findings.implicationForProject: Show a persistent 'consult your doctor / not a diagnosis' disclaimer in Arabic and English on the AI assistant and any wound-assessment screens. Do not claim the camera or AI can measure or diagnose wounds unless the methodology is validated and documented. If an Egyptian Drug Authority (or other) clearance exists, put the link in the App Review notes. Otherwise present AI output as informational.

findings.requirement: 1.4.2: Drug dosage calculators must come from the drug manufacturer, a hospital, university, health insurer, pharmacy or other approved entity, or be approved by the FDA or an international counterpart.
findings.sourceQuote: Drug dosage calculators must come from the drug manufacturer, a hospital, university, health insurance company, pharmacy or other approved entity, or receive approval by the FDA or one of its international counterparts.
findings.implicationForProject: Do not let the AI assistant or any tool compute medication or dressing dosages unless TetraSol (as manufacturer) or an approved entity provides and stands behind it. Gate it behind a feature flag.

findings.requirement: 5.1.1(ix): Apps that provide services in highly regulated fields, explicitly including healthcare, should be submitted by a legal entity that provides the services, not an individual developer.
findings.sourceQuote: Apps that provide services in highly regulated fields (such as banking and financial services, healthcare, gambling, legal cannabis use, air travel and crypto exchanges) or that require sensitive user information should be submitted by a legal entity that provides the services, and not by an individual developer.
findings.implicationForProject: Enroll the Apple Developer account as an Organization, under the legal entity (e.g. Alia Group / the operating company) that actually provides the healthcare marketplace service. A personal (individual) developer account is likely to be rejected.

findings.requirement: Organization enrollment requires: a legal entity that can contract with Apple (no DBAs, trade names or branches); a D-U-N-S Number; an enrolling person with legal binding authority; and a public, functional website on a domain associated with the organization. The fee is 99 USD per year, shown in local currency. The organization's name appears as the seller on the App Store.
findings.sourceQuote: Your organization (excluding government entities) must have a D-U-N-S Number... Your organization's website must be publicly available and functional, and its domain name must be associated with your organization.
findings.implicationForProject: Get a D-U-N-S number for the Egyptian legal entity and a real company website, with privacy policy and terms, before iOS submission. Plan for D&B lead time.

findings.requirement: 5.1.3: Health, fitness and medical data may not be used or disclosed to third parties for advertising, marketing or data-mining, except to improve health management or for health research, and then only with permission. Apps must disclose the specific health data collected from the device, must not write false data into HealthKit, and may not store personal health information in iCloud. Human-subject research needs informed consent and ethics-board approval.
findings.sourceQuote: Apps may not use or disclose to third parties data gathered in the health, fitness, and medical research context... for advertising, marketing, or other use-based data mining purposes other than improving health management, or for the purpose of health research, and then only with permission... and may not store personal health information in iCloud.
findings.implicationForProject: Keep wound photos and clinical notes out of analytics and ad SDKs. Do not use health data to market TetraSol products without explicit opt-in. Disable iCloud backup for local PHI (exclude files from backup; avoid iCloud key-value or CloudKit). Keep any research use behind a separate consent.

findings.requirement: 5.1.2(i): Apps must clearly disclose where personal data will be shared with third parties, including third-party AI, and obtain explicit permission before doing so.
findings.sourceQuote: You must clearly disclose where personal data will be shared with third parties, including with third-party AI, and obtain explicit permission before doing so.
findings.implicationForProject: Before the AI assistant sends any patient data or wound images to an external LLM provider, show an explicit consent screen that names the provider category. Store the consent, allow revocation, and list the provider in the privacy policy and privacy nutrition label.

findings.requirement: 5.1.1(i) and (v): A privacy policy link is required both in App Store Connect and inside the app. It must cover data collected, third-party sharing, retention and deletion, and how to revoke consent. Apps that support account creation must offer account deletion within the app.
findings.sourceQuote: If your app supports account creation, you must also offer account deletion within the app.
findings.implicationForProject: Provide an in-app privacy policy link and an in-app 'Delete account' flow for all three roles (patient, doctor, nurse).

findings.requirement: Apple's account-deletion guidance: apps in highly regulated industries under 5.1.1(ix) may use extra customer-service flows to confirm deletion. The app must tell users what data is legally retained. If an auto-renewable subscription is active, it must tell users that billing continues through Apple and ask them to cancel. Deletion may be scheduled for subscription expiry only if immediate deletion is also offered. Apps using Sign in with Apple must revoke tokens via the REST API.
findings.sourceQuote: Apps in highly regulated industries, as described in App Review Guideline 5.1.1(ix), may use additional customer service flows to confirm and facilitate the account deletion process... If a person has an auto-renewable subscription, notify them that billing will continue through Apple and ask them to cancel their subscription before continuing.
findings.implicationForProject: The deletion flow may include a verification step for clinicians and medical-record retention, but must be started in-app. Show which medical and transaction records are retained under Egyptian law. Warn iOS subscribers and deep-link to Manage Subscriptions.

findings.requirement: 3.1.1: Unlocking features or functionality in the app, including subscriptions and premium content, must use In-App Purchase. Apps may not use their own unlock mechanisms (license keys, QR codes, etc.). Apps should provide a restore mechanism for restorable IAPs.
findings.sourceQuote: If you want to unlock features or functionality within your app, (by way of example: subscriptions, in-game currencies, game levels, access to premium content, or unlocking a full version), you must use in-app purchase... you should make sure you have a restore mechanism for any restorable in-app purchases.
findings.implicationForProject: On iOS, any purchase that unlocks the AI assistant or other in-app digital features (e.g. Silver/Gold/Platinum) must be sold via StoreKit IAP, not Paymob. Add a 'Restore Purchases' button. Paymob must never unlock digital features on iOS.

findings.requirement: 3.1.3(e): Physical goods, or services consumed outside the app, must use purchase methods other than IAP, such as Apple Pay or credit card entry.
findings.sourceQuote: If your app enables people to purchase physical goods or services that will be consumed outside of the app, you must use purchase methods other than in-app purchase to collect those payments, such as Apple Pay or traditional credit card entry.
findings.implicationForProject: The TetraSol physical product store and payment for in-person nurse or doctor visits must use Paymob (card or wallet), possibly Apple Pay. They must not use IAP. App Review flags IAP products for these as a violation.

findings.requirement: 3.1.3(d): Real-time person-to-person services between two individuals, explicitly including medical consultations, may use non-IAP payment. One-to-few and one-to-many real-time services must use IAP.
findings.sourceQuote: If your app enables the purchase of real-time person-to-person services between two individuals (for example tutoring students, medical consultations, real estate tours, or fitness training), you may use purchase methods other than in-app purchase to collect those payments. One-to-few and one-to-many real-time services must use in-app purchase.
findings.implicationForProject: Live 1:1 video or chat consultations with a doctor or nurse may be billed via Paymob. Group webinars or classes, recorded content, or async AI consultations would need IAP. Classify each service type in the payment-classification service.

findings.requirement: 3.1.3 intro: Apps using other purchase methods under 3.1.3 cannot, within the app, encourage users to use a purchase method other than IAP. Exceptions are the US storefront and the cases in 3.1.1(a)/3.1.3(a). Developers may communicate about other methods outside the app.
findings.sourceQuote: Apps in this section cannot, within the app, encourage users to use a purchasing method other than in-app purchase, except for apps on the United States storefront and as set forth in 3.1.1(a) and 3.1.3(a). Developers can send communications outside of the app to their user base about purchasing methods other than in-app purchase.
findings.implicationForProject: On the Egypt iOS build, never show 'subscribe cheaper on our website / via Paymob' for digital tiers. Do not price-steer IAP items to Paymob. Email or SMS outside the app is allowed.

findings.requirement: 3.1.1/3.1.1(a): The StoreKit External Purchase Link Entitlement is limited to specific storefronts. In all other storefronts except the US, apps and metadata may not include buttons, external links or calls to action pointing to non-IAP purchasing.
findings.sourceQuote: The entitlements are limited to use only in the iOS or iPadOS App Store in specific storefronts. In all other storefronts, except for the United States storefront, where this prohibition does not apply, apps and their metadata may not include buttons, external links, or other calls to action that direct customers to purchasing mechanisms other than in-app purchase.
findings.implicationForProject: Egypt is not the US storefront, so link-outs for digital subscriptions are prohibited in the Egypt iOS app and its App Store metadata.

findings.requirement: The valid storefront country codes for the External Purchase Link entitlement are the 27 EU countries plus Iceland (is), Norway (no) and Russia (ru). The External Purchase (alternative payment) entitlement covers the EU plus South Korea (kr). Egypt (eg) is in neither list. The Developer Program License Agreement has separate alternative-payment terms only for Japan and Brazil (Attachment 12), China mainland (Attachment 13) and the EU (Attachment 14, effective Oct 1, 2026).
findings.sourceQuote: Valid country codes include those for the European Union: Austria (at)... Sweden (se); and Iceland (is), Norway (no), and Russia (ru).
findings.implicationForProject: Egypt is NOT eligible for an external purchase link or for alternative payment processing. On iOS in Egypt, digital subscriptions must use IAP only. Do not add SKExternalPurchase or SKExternalPurchaseLink plist keys or entitlements.

findings.requirement: 3.1.3(b) Multiplatform: content or subscriptions bought on other platforms or the website can be accessed in the iOS app only if those items are also available as IAP within the app.
findings.sourceQuote: Apps that operate across multiple platforms may allow users to access content, subscriptions, or features they have acquired in your app on other platforms or your web site... provided those items are also available as in-app purchases within the app.
findings.implicationForProject: A Silver/Gold/Platinum plan bought via Paymob on Android or web may be honored on iOS only if the same tiers are also offered as IAP on iOS. The backend entitlement service must merge Paymob and App Store entitlements per user.

findings.requirement: 3.1.2(a): Auto-renewable subscriptions must provide ongoing value, last at least 7 days, and be available on all of the user's devices. They may include access to discounted consumable goods. Bait-and-switch or false-pretense subscriptions are removed.
findings.sourceQuote: If you offer an auto-renewable subscription, you must provide ongoing value to the customer, and the subscription period must last at least seven days and be available across all of the user's devices.
findings.implicationForProject: Each tier needs genuine ongoing value: AI assistant usage, continuously updated content and priority features. The minimum period is weekly; monthly or annual is recommended.

findings.requirement: 3.1.2(b) and (c): Upgrades and downgrades must be seamless, with no accidental duplicate subscriptions (use one subscription group). Before asking to subscribe, the app must clearly describe what the user gets for the price and meet Schedule 2. Schedule 2 §3.8(b) requires clearly and conspicuously disclosing the title, length and price (and price per unit if appropriate), with links to the Privacy Policy and Terms of Use accessible in the app.
findings.sourceQuote: (b) You clearly and conspicuously disclose to users the following information regarding Your auto- renewing subscription: Title of auto-renewing subscription... Length of subscription Price of subscription, and price per unit if appropriate Links to Your Privacy Policy and Terms of Use must be accessible within Your Licensed Application.
findings.implicationForProject: Put Silver, Gold and Platinum in a single subscription group, ranked by level. The paywall must show the tier name, duration, full localized EGP price, the benefits per tier, and Terms and Privacy links. Add the Terms of Use (EULA) link to the App Store description too.

findings.requirement: Apple's subscription sign-up screen requirements: subscription name, duration and content or services; the full renewal price shown clearly and prominently, localized; and a way for existing subscribers to sign in or restore purchases. The billed amount must be the most prominent pricing element. Free trials must state their length and the post-trial price. Apple recommends showManageSubscriptions for in-app management and an easy path to cancel.
findings.sourceQuote: the following details must be included in your subscription's sign-up screen: Subscription name and duration, and the content or services provided during the subscription period; Full renewal price, shown clearly and prominently, and localized in available currencies; A way for current subscribers to sign in or restore purchases
findings.implicationForProject: The paywall UI needs a 'Restore purchases' button and the billed amount as the largest price element. Any per-month equivalent must be visually subordinate. Add a 'Manage subscription' entry that opens Apple's management sheet.

findings.requirement: No official Apple guidance covers a subscription that bundles in-app digital features with real-world service benefits. 3.1.1 requires IAP for unlocking in-app features and functionality. 3.1.3(e) requires non-IAP for services consumed outside the app. A 2022 developer-forum question on exactly this mixed case (a gym membership with physical and digital benefits) got no Apple answer.
findings.sourceQuote: (3.1.1) If you want to unlock features or functionality within your app... you must use in-app purchase. / (3.1.3(e)) ...physical goods or services that will be consumed outside of the app, you must use purchase methods other than in-app purchase
findings.implicationForProject: Safest design, given the AI assistant is a digital in-app feature: sell Silver/Gold/Platinum on iOS via IAP as the single subscription, including the bundled real-world perks (priority matching, reduced platform fee). Charge the in-person visit itself via Paymob, with the tier discount applied server-side. Do not sell the tiers via Paymob in the iOS app. Alternative: split into an IAP 'AI/digital' subscription and a separately sold service plan with no digital unlocks. Confirm with App Review in the review notes or via Apple's App Review contact.

findings.requirement: 2.1(a)/(b): Include demo account information for apps with login, with the backend running. A built-in demo mode needs Apple's prior approval. IAPs must be complete, visible to the reviewer and functional.
findings.sourceQuote: include demo account info (and turn on your back-end service!) if your app includes a login... If you offer in-app purchases in your app, make sure they are complete, up-to-date, visible to the reviewer and functional.
findings.implicationForProject: Provide review accounts for patient, doctor and nurse (pre-verified clinician status) in the review notes. Configure sandbox IAP for all three tiers. Explain in the notes which purchases use Paymob under 3.1.3(d)/(e).

findings.requirement: Regulated medical device status: apps distributed in the EEA, UK or US must declare their status in App Store Connect if their primary or secondary category is Health & Fitness or Medical, or if they answered 'frequent' for Medical or Treatment Information in the age rating. New apps must declare from March 26, 2026. Existing apps must declare by early 2027 or they can no longer submit updates. The requirement does not cover Egypt.
findings.sourceQuote: Starting today, this status is required for new apps that meet either of the criteria above in order to distribute in these regions. Existing apps distributed in these regions that meet either of the criteria above must provide a status by early 2027.
findings.implicationForProject: If availability is Egypt-only, no declaration is needed. If the app is also offered in the EEA, UK or US with the Medical or Health & Fitness category, the Account Holder or Admin must declare 'No' (or 'Yes' with regulatory details) under App Information > App Store Regulations & Permits before release.

findings.requirement: Under the Developer Program License Agreement, Egypt is a region where Apple Distribution International acts as commissionaire. Under Exhibit B, Apple collects and remits applicable taxes on App Store sales to end users in Egypt.
findings.sourceQuote: Apple shall collect and remit to the competent tax authorities the taxes described in Section 3.2 of Schedule 2 for sales of the Licensed Applications to End-Users... located in the following regions... Egypt
findings.implicationForProject: Apple handles tax on IAP subscription revenue in Egypt. The company handles tax and invoicing for Paymob sales (products and visits) itself. Keep the two revenue streams separate in accounting.

unresolved: Apple has published no official rule for subscriptions that mix digital features (AI assistant) with real-world benefits (priority matching, reduced platform fees on in-person visits). The forum question (thread 698791) has no Apple answer. Get written clarification from App Review before launch.
Whether 'priority matching' counts as an in-app feature (needs IAP) or as part of an out-of-app service (3.1.3(e)) is not settled by the guideline text.
If teleconsultations are added: whether async chat or AI-plus-clinician hybrid consults qualify as 'real-time person-to-person' under 3.1.3(d) is not defined by Apple.
Egyptian regulatory clearance (e.g. Egyptian Drug Authority) for wound-assessment or AI features, to cite under 1.4.1, was not verified in this topic.
Apple gives no exact date for the 'early 2027' deadline for existing apps to declare regulated medical device status (only relevant if distributed in the EEA, UK or US).
The commission rate for IAP subscriptions in Egypt (Small Business Program 15% / standard 30% / 15% after year one) was not re-verified here.

The StoreKit ExternalPurchase/ExternalPurchaseLink documentation pages list the EU, South Korea, the Netherlands (dating), Russia and the EEA (music). The license agreement also has Japan/Brazil and US-storefront provisions. None covers Egypt, but Apple says the lists are 'updated from time to time'.

research.topic: google-technical: Google Play technical requirements as of 2026-10-14 (target API, 16 KB pages, 64-bit, AAB, Play App Signing, edge-to-edge, predictive back) for Expo SDK 57 / RN 0.86

findings.requirement: Target API level: starting August 31, 2026, new apps and app updates must target Android 16 (API level 36) or higher to be submitted to Google Play. Wear OS and Android Automotive OS apps need API 35, and Android TV and Android XR apps need API 34. Developers can request an extension to November 1, 2026. The only exception is permanently private, organization-internal apps. The user's claim (API 36, Aug 31 2026) is correct.
findings.sourceQuote: Starting August 31 2026: New apps and app updates must target Android 16 (API level 36) or higher to be submitted to Google Play ... If you need more time to update your app, you'll be able to request an extension to November 1, 2026.
findings.implicationForProject: Today (2026-10-14) is past the deadline. Every Dress My Wound AAB uploaded to Play must have targetSdkVersion 36 or higher. Expo SDK 57 defaults to targetSdk 36 and the project inherits it through rootProject.ext.targetSdkVersion. Do not lower it through expo-build-properties. Confirm targetSdk=36 in the merged manifest of the built AAB (for example with aapt2 or bundletool dump manifest) before submitting.

findings.requirement: Existing-app availability rule: from Aug 31, 2026, existing apps must target API 35 or higher to stay available to new users on devices running an Android version newer than the app's target. This is mirrored in the Play Console Help article on target API level.
findings.sourceQuote: Existing apps must target Android 15 (API level 35) or higher to remain available to new users
findings.implicationForProject: This does not apply to a new listing, which must target 36 anyway. Keep targetSdk current every year so older releases are not hidden from new users.

findings.requirement: Expo SDK 57 (React Native 0.86) ships with compileSdkVersion 36 and targetSdkVersion 36 and supports Android 7 and later. The React Native 0.86.3 version catalog found locally lists minSdk 24, targetSdk 36, compileSdk 36, AGP 8.12.0 and NDK 27.1.12297006.
findings.implicationForProject: The default toolchain meets the API 36 requirement with no overrides. AGP 8.12.0 is above the 8.5.1 minimum needed for 16 KB zip alignment of uncompressed .so files.

findings.requirement: 16 KB memory page size: all apps targeting Android 15 (API 35) or higher must support 16 KB pages on 64-bit devices on Google Play. The current Android developer page says that from February 1, 2027, app updates without 16 KB support cannot be released. The May 2025 Android Developers Blog originally gave November 1, 2025 for new apps and updates. The Play Console technical quality page lists 16 KB support under current requirements for new app bundles.
findings.effectiveDate: Originally 2025-11-01 (blog); updates blocked from 2027-02-01 (current dev page, last updated 2026-09-16)
findings.sourceQuote: all apps targeting Android 15 (API level 35) and higher must support 16 KB memory page sizes on 64-bit devices on Google Play. Starting February 1, 2027, if your app updates don't support 16 KB memory page sizes, you won't be able to release these updates.
findings.implicationForProject: Treat 16 KB support as required now for the first AAB upload. The Play Console technical page says new app bundles must support it, and a community Product Expert says new apps get no grace period. The app has native code from React Native, Hermes, Expo modules and any native SDKs, so every .so in the AAB must be 16 KB aligned and zip-aligned.

findings.requirement: Play Console technical quality requirements, current requirements section: apps that contain native code must support 64-bit-only architectures and 16 KB memory page sizes, and new app bundles uploaded to Play Console must support them.
findings.sourceQuote: new app bundles uploaded to Play Console must support them. 64-bit support: Apps that contain native code must support 64-bit only architectures. 16 KB memory page size support: Apps that contain native code must support devices with 16 KB memory page sizes.
findings.implicationForProject: Both checks are gates on upload. Ship arm64-v8a (and x86_64 if x86 is included) and confirm 16 KB alignment before uploading to the internal track.

findings.requirement: How to verify 16 KB alignment: (1) run check_elf_alignment.sh APK_NAME.apk, which prints ALIGNED or UNALIGNED for arm64-v8a libraries; (2) run `llvm-objdump -p LIB.so | grep LOAD` and check every LOAD segment shows align 2**14 or higher (2**13 or 2**12 means it fails); (3) run `zipalign -v -c -P 16 4 APK_NAME.apk` (build-tools 35.0.0 or later), whose last line should read 'Verification successful'; (4) for an AAB, run `bundletool dump config --bundle=<aab> | grep alignment` and expect PAGE_ALIGNMENT_16K; (5) optionally test on a 16 KB emulator image, where `adb shell getconf PAGE_SIZE` returns 16384.
findings.sourceQuote: If any load segments are 2**13, 2**12, or lower values, you'll need to update the packaging for those libraries ... The last line of the output will say 'Verification successful' if all of the shared libraries are aligned correctly. ... If you see PAGE_ALIGNMENT_16K then you know your bundle requests 16 KB zip alignment.
findings.implicationForProject: Add these checks to the Android build verification (task #6) and CI: (a) bundletool alignment check on the production AAB; (b) build universal APKs from the AAB with bundletool and run zipalign -c -P 16 and check_elf_alignment.sh; (c) run llvm-objdump on every lib/arm64-v8a/*.so. The project already sets expo.useLegacyPackaging=false, so libraries stay uncompressed and need 16 KB zip alignment, which AGP 8.12 provides.

findings.requirement: 16 KB toolchain: AGP 8.5.1 or later is needed for 16 KB zip alignment of uncompressed shared libraries. NDK r28 and later compile 16 KB-aligned by default. NDK r27 and earlier need the linker flags -Wl,-z,max-page-size=16384 and -Wl,-z,common-page-size=16384. React Native 0.77 and later fully support 16 KB page size.
findings.sourceQuote: With the 0.77 release, React Native is ready to fully support 16 KB page size and developers will be able to test and ship apps for 16 KB devices using it.
findings.implicationForProject: React Native 0.86 core is supported. The local RN catalog pins NDK 27.1, so any custom C/C++ or third-party library compiled from source must pass the 16 KB flags (or use NDK r28 or later). Prebuilt .so files from third-party SDKs (payments, analytics, video, image processing) are the main risk; run the alignment checks on the final AAB.

findings.requirement: 64-bit: apps published on Google Play must support 64-bit architectures. For each native 32-bit ABI shipped, the matching 64-bit ABI must also be included (armeabi-v7a needs arm64-v8a; x86 needs x86_64). Apps with only Java or Kotlin code are compliant automatically.
findings.effectiveDate: In force (the exact original date is not on the current page)
findings.sourceQuote: It isn't required to support every 64-bit architecture, but for each native 32-bit architecture you support you must include the corresponding 64-bit architecture.
findings.implicationForProject: Keep the default reactNativeArchitectures (armeabi-v7a, arm64-v8a, x86, x86_64) or at least arm64-v8a. Never ship a 32-bit-only ABI filter.

findings.requirement: Android App Bundle: starting August 2021, new apps must publish with the Android App Bundle on Google Play. New apps larger than 200 MB can use Play Asset Delivery or Play Feature Delivery. Since June 30, 2023, TV app updates must also use AAB. App bundles do not support OBB expansion files. The total compressed download (base plus config APKs) must be 4 GB or less.
findings.sourceQuote: Starting August 2021, new apps are required to publish with the Android App Bundle on Google Play.
findings.implicationForProject: The eas.json production and preview-store profiles already use android.buildType "app-bundle". Keep APKs (development and preview profiles) for internal sideload or testing only. Never upload an APK to Play for this new app.

findings.requirement: Play App Signing: app bundles require enrollment in Play App Signing. The developer keeps an upload key (RSA, 2048 bits or more), which Google can reset if lost. Google holds the app signing key: Google-generated keys are RSA 4096, and custom keys must be RSA 2048 or more. For new apps, uploading a bundle enrolls the app by default in 'quantum-ready, hybrid signing with Google-generated keys'. Developers can switch to their own key only before a release reaches open testing or production. Key upgrades are available, with enforcement on Android 17 (API 37) and later.
findings.sourceQuote: To use app bundles, you must enroll in Play App Signing (answer/9844279) ... By default, when you upload your app bundle, your app is automatically enrolled in quantum-ready, hybrid signing with Google-generated keys.
findings.implicationForProject: The keystore generated by EAS is the upload key only. Back up its credentials (eas credentials) and accept the Google-generated app signing key. Decide on the key choice before the first open-testing or production release, because it cannot be changed afterwards. For Google Sign-In, Firebase or Maps API restrictions, register the Play app-signing certificate SHA-1/SHA-256 from Play Console (App integrity), not just the upload key's fingerprint.

findings.requirement: Edge-to-edge (targetSdk 35 on Android 15): apps are edge-to-edge by default. The status bar and gesture navigation bar are transparent, content draws behind the system bars unless insets are applied, and setStatusBarColor and setNavigationBarColor are deprecated (statusBarColor has no effect). The 3-button nav bar is 80% opaque by default. Display cutout mode is forced to ALWAYS.
findings.effectiveDate: For any build targeting API 35 or higher
findings.sourceQuote: Apps are edge-to-edge by default on devices running Android 15 if the app is targeting Android 15 (API level 35). ... This is a breaking change that might negatively impact your app's UI.
findings.implicationForProject: Every screen (patient, doctor and nurse flows, store, checkout, Paymob webview, chat, AI assistant) must handle insets with react-native-safe-area-context (~5.7). Bottom CTAs and keyboard-avoiding inputs need safe-area bottom padding. Do not rely on androidStatusBar.backgroundColor or navigation-bar colors.

findings.requirement: Android 16 (targetSdk 36): the edge-to-edge opt-out is removed. R.attr#windowOptOutEdgeToEdgeEnforcement is deprecated and disabled, so apps cannot opt out of edge-to-edge. Expo SDK 54 and later: 'edge-to-edge will be enabled in all Android apps, and cannot be disabled'. Expo SDK 55 removed the edgeToEdgeEnabled app.json option and turned most expo-navigation-bar color and behavior methods into no-ops.
findings.effectiveDate: For any build targeting API 36 (required for Play since 2026-08-31)
