findings.sourceQuote: For apps targeting Android 16 (API level 36), R.attr#windowOptOutEdgeToEdgeEnforcement is deprecated and disabled, and your app can't opt-out of going edge-to-edge.
findings.implicationForProject: Edge-to-edge is mandatory for Dress My Wound. Remove any windowOptOutEdgeToEdgeEnforcement theme item or expo-navigation-bar color calls. The edgeToEdgeEnabled=true in android/gradle.properties is consistent and harmless. Test RTL Arabic layouts with gesture and 3-button navigation.

findings.requirement: Predictive back (targetSdk 36 on Android 16 or later devices): predictive back system animations (back-to-home, cross-task, cross-activity) are on by default. Activity.onBackPressed is not called and KeyEvent.KEYCODE_BACK is no longer dispatched. Apps that intercept back must migrate to the supported APIs (OnBackPressedCallback or OnBackInvokedCallback), or temporarily opt out with android:enableOnBackInvokedCallback="false". Even when that is set to false, OnBackPressedCallback is always called. This is a platform behavior change; I found no separate Play requirement for it.
findings.sourceQuote: For apps targeting Android 16 (API level 36) or higher and running on an Android 16 or higher device, the predictive back system animations (back-to-home, cross-task, and cross-activity) are enabled by default. Additionally, onBackPressed is not called and KeyEvent.KEYCODE_BACK is not dispatched anymore.
findings.implicationForProject: Expo's android.predictiveBackGestureEnabled defaults to false, which writes enableOnBackInvokedCallback="false" (confirmed in the config-plugins source). This project sets predictiveBackGestureEnabled: true, and the manifest has enableOnBackInvokedCallback="true". So any back interception (unsaved wound-photo or consent forms, checkout and Paymob flows, exit-confirmation dialogs) must go through supported APIs (React Native BackHandler or react-navigation beforeRemove, if they use OnBackPressedCallback), never onBackPressed or KEYCODE_BACK. No BackHandler use was found in src/. Test on a real Android 16 device. If problems appear, set predictiveBackGestureEnabled: false as the documented temporary opt-out.

findings.requirement: Android 16 (targetSdk 36): on displays with smallest width of 600dp or more (tablets, unfolded foldables), orientation, resizability and aspect-ratio restrictions are ignored. There is a temporary opt-out through the PROPERTY_COMPAT_ALLOW_RESTRICTED_RESIZABILITY manifest property. The Android 17 page says this opt-out is gone for apps targeting API 37.
findings.effectiveDate: API 36 targeting (now); opt-out removed at API 37 targeting
findings.sourceQuote: Developers have the option to opt out of these changes with SDK 36, but this opt-out will no longer be available for apps that target Android 17 (API level 37) or higher.
findings.implicationForProject: app.config.ts sets orientation 'portrait' (screenOrientation="portrait"), but this lock will be ignored on tablets and foldables. Doctor and nurse users on tablets will see landscape and resizable windows, so layouts must adapt (flex and useWindowDimensions, no fixed-height portrait assumptions). The opt-out should be treated as temporary only.

findings.requirement: Text rendering for Arabic: for apps targeting API 35, the TextView elegantTextHeight attribute defaults to true (the taller, more readable font instead of the compact font). Android 16 deprecates elegantTextHeight and ignores it once the app targets API 36. Android 15 also reserves a locale-based minimum line height in EditText.
findings.sourceQuote: Android 16 deprecates the elegantTextHeight attribute, and the attribute will be ignored once your app targets Android 16.
findings.implicationForProject: The Arabic (غير لي) UI will use the elegant (taller) line metrics with no way back to compact. Verify that Arabic text in buttons, chips, tab bars, price labels and inputs is not clipped. Avoid fixed heights and tight lineHeight values in the design system.

findings.requirement: Upcoming Play technical quality requirements (announced Aug 26, 2026): from February 2027, (a) new memory-usage bad-behavior thresholds (Anon RSS + Swap, and bitmap memory) per RAM tier, for phones and tablets; (b) a DEX code-optimization minimum of 25% obfuscation, optimization and shrinking (for example with R8) for apps with more than 10 MB of DEX. From April 2027, apps with sign-in must support zero-tap sign-in restoration (Restore Credentials API). Apps under strict regulatory constraints 'such as financial services or healthcare' may request an exemption through Play Console before enforcement.
findings.sourceQuote: From February 2027, apps and games on Google Play will need to meet minimum optimization requirements. You will need to achieve a minimum of 25% optimization, obfuscation and shrinking for any app uploads to Play Console. ... Apps subject to strict regulatory or compliance mandates that impact how your sign-in feature works (such as financial services or healthcare) may be eligible for an exemption.
findings.implicationForProject: (1) android/app/build.gradle has minify off by default (android.enableMinifyInReleaseBuilds false). Check DEX size in Play's app bundle explorer, and if it exceeds 10 MB, enable R8 (expo-build-properties enableMinifyInReleaseBuilds/enableShrinkResourcesInReleaseBuilds) with keep rules before Feb 2027. (2) Decide whether to implement the Restore Credentials API for patient, doctor and nurse sessions, or to file a healthcare exemption request in Play Console before April 2027. (3) Watch memory vitals for image-heavy wound-photo screens.

unresolved: 16 KB timeline conflict: the May 2025 Android blog says Nov 1, 2025 for new apps and updates. Forum-quoted Play emails mention an extension to May 31, 2026. The current developer page (updated 2026-09-16) says app updates are blocked from Feb 1, 2027. I found no official announcement explaining the move to Feb 2027, and no official text on whether a brand-new app (as opposed to an update) is blocked at upload today. The Play Console technical page's 'new app bundles uploaded to Play Console must support them' and a community Product Expert both suggest yes. Treat it as required now.

I could not confirm that every native library in this project's dependency tree is 16 KB aligned. The RN 0.86.3 catalog pins NDK 27.1.12297006, so libraries built from source depend on the linker flags. This needs an actual AAB build plus bundletool, zipalign and llvm-objdump checks (task #6).

Not verified from source: whether React Native 0.86's BackHandler and the react-navigation/expo-router back handling use androidx OnBackPressedCallback (works with predictive back) rather than onBackPressed/KEYCODE_BACK (not delivered at targetSdk 36 with enableOnBackInvokedCallback=true). The project sets predictiveBackGestureEnabled: true. Needs an on-device Android 16 test.

I found no Google Play policy or Play Console requirement that mandates predictive back support. It is only a platform behavior change at targetSdk 36. Expo's SDK 54 changelog expected to enable it by default 'in SDK 55 or 56', but the latest Expo app-config docs still say 'Default to false'.

Target API extension forms: the developer page still says extension forms will be available 'later this year'. I did not verify whether they are open in Play Console now, but a new app on Expo SDK 57 (targetSdk 36) does not need one.
I could not find the original date of the 64-bit requirement (August 1, 2019) on the current official 64-bit page. It is in force, and the original date is not material.
This app's DEX size is unknown, so I cannot say whether the Feb 2027 25% optimization requirement (apps with more than 10 MB DEX) will apply. Check the app bundle explorer after the first upload.

research.topic: google-policy: Google Play Payments/Billing (Egypt), Play Billing Library version, Health apps policy & declaration, organization accounts, Data safety, account deletion, photo/video and location permissions, target audience, closed-testing rule for new personal accounts (verified 2026-10-14)

findings.requirement: Physical goods and physical services must NOT go through Google Play's billing system. Section 3 of the Payments policy forbids it when payment is primarily for physical goods or physical services.
findings.sourceQuote: Google Play's billing system must not be used in cases where: payment is primarily: for the purchase or rental of physical goods (such as groceries, clothing, housewares, electronics); for the purchase of physical services (such as transportation services, cleaning services, airfare, gym memberships, food delivery, tickets for live events)
findings.implicationForProject: Charge for TetraSol store items and in-person nurse or doctor visits through Paymob, never through Play Billing. Mark these as physical in the payment classification layer and keep them off the IAP code path.

findings.requirement: Transactions for regulated clinical services should not use Play Billing. These are services provided by or on behalf of a licensed healthcare provider to diagnose or manage medical conditions, such as consulting a doctor, receiving a prescription, or treatment planning.
findings.sourceQuote: Transactions involving regulated clinical services should not use Google Play's billing system. Regulated clinical services include services provided by or on behalf of a licensed healthcare provider that is intended to diagnose or manage (prevent, treat, mitigate, or cure) medical conditions.
findings.implicationForProject: Doctor consultations, wound-care treatment planning and nurse wound dressing by licensed professionals can be charged through Paymob, including remote consults. The Health Content and Services policy page repeats this rule under 'Payments - Clinical Services'.

findings.requirement: 1:1 online paid services between two individuals that are not available for replay do not require Play Billing. Health coaching and counseling are among the listed examples.
findings.sourceQuote: If your app provides a 1:1 online paid service, you are not required to use Google Play's billing system if: the paid service is between two individuals; the paid service is not available for replay afterwards
findings.implicationForProject: Live video or chat sessions with a doctor or nurse can stay on Paymob. If sessions are recorded and can be replayed in the app, this exemption no longer applies, so rely on the clinical-services exemption instead.

findings.requirement: For SKUs that mix digital and physical value, Play Billing is required when the SKU includes more digital than physical goods or services, or when it is marketed as digital.
findings.sourceQuote: Google Play's billing system must be used for the SKUs in your app that include more digital goods or services than physical goods or services, and for the SKUs in your app that are marketed to users as digital goods or services.
findings.implicationForProject: Silver, Gold and Platinum mix an AI assistant (digital) with priority matching and reduced platform fees on in-person visits. Priority matching is arguably an in-app digital feature. A tier marketed around the AI assistant would most likely need Play Billing on Android. Safest design: (a) sell the AI and digital features as Play Billing subscriptions through an entitlement service, and (b) build real-world benefits into Paymob-charged visit pricing. Alternatively, get written confirmation from Play policy support before charging hybrid tiers through Paymob. Section 4 also bans in-app links or buttons that lead to Paymob for digital SKUs.

findings.requirement: Apps may not steer users to a payment method other than Play Billing for in-app digital purchases. This covers webviews, buttons, links, messaging and sign-up flows. The exceptions are Section 3 (physical goods and services) and Sections 8/9 (enrolled alternative billing or external-link programs in eligible regions).
findings.sourceQuote: Other than the conditions described in Section 3, Section 8, and Section 9, apps may not lead users to a payment method other than Google Play's billing system.
findings.implicationForProject: On Android, the subscription screen must not show a 'pay with card/Paymob' option or a web link for the digital tiers. In-app pricing must match the price on the Play billing sheet (Section 6).

findings.requirement: Play purchases (paid apps, in-app products, subscriptions) are supported for buyers in Egypt, in EGP from 0.90 to 49,000.00. Egypt is also a supported developer and merchant registration location; developers there are paid in USD or EUR.
findings.sourceQuote: Egypt (EG) | Download free apps ✓ | Make Google Play purchases ✓ | EGP 0.90 - 49,000.00 ("Listed price ranges apply to paid apps, in-app products and subscriptions")
findings.implicationForProject: Play Billing is live in Egypt, so the Play Billing requirement for digital SKUs applies there in full. The exemption for countries where Play Billing has not launched does not help. Set EGP subscription prices within this range. Merchant-registration source: https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/9306917 ('Egypt ✔ ✔ EGP').

findings.requirement: No user choice billing, alternative billing or billing choice program is currently open to users in Egypt. Today these cover the EEA, UK, US, AU, JP, KR, IN, BR, ID and ZA. Under Google's new fee model, 'Expanded Billing Choice Availability' reaches 'Rest of World' on September 30, 2027.
findings.sourceQuote: September 30, 2027 | Rest of World | Rest of World ... For transactions that use Google Play Billing, an additional billing fee applies. In the AU, JP, US, UK, and the European Economic Area (EEA), the billing fee is set at 5%. Billing fee details for other regions are forthcoming.
findings.implicationForProject: Until at least 2027-09-30, Paymob cannot be offered as an alternative for digital subscriptions to Egyptian users. Revisit this when the Rest of World rollout happens. Program lists: https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/13821247 and https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/17161464.

findings.requirement: Play Billing Library deprecation: Version 7's new-app/update deadline was Aug 31, 2026, with extension to Nov 1, 2026. From then on, new apps and updates must use PBL 8 or later. Version 8 is deprecated on Aug 31, 2027 (extension to Nov 1, 2027). The latest release is PBL 9.1.0 (2026-06-18).
findings.sourceQuote: Reminder: By Aug 31, 2026, all new apps and updates to existing apps must use Billing Library version 8 or later. If you need more time to update your app, you can request an extension until Nov 1, 2026.
findings.implicationForProject: Whichever React Native IAP layer is used (expo-iap, react-native-iap or RevenueCat) must bundle PBL 8 or later; prefer PBL 9.x (release notes: https://developer.android.com/google/play/billing/release-notes) so you are not deprecated again on 2027-08-31. In the EAS-built AAB, check that the merged AndroidManifest contains com.google.android.play.billingclient.version.

findings.requirement: Target API level: from Aug 31, 2026, new apps and updates must target Android 16 (API 36) or higher, with extension to Nov 1, 2026. Existing apps must target API 35 or higher to stay available to new users.
findings.sourceQuote: New apps and app updates must target Android 16 (API level 36) or higher to be submitted to Google Play
findings.implicationForProject: Confirm that the Expo SDK 57 / RN 0.86 build has targetSdkVersion 36 or higher (expo-build-properties if needed) before the first Play submission.

findings.requirement: Health Content and Services policy, part 1. Every health or medical app must: complete the Health apps declaration (Policy > App content); link a privacy policy both in Play Console and inside the app (active, public, non-geofenced, non-PDF URL); and comprehensively disclose collection and sharing of personal or sensitive data.
findings.sourceQuote: All developers must complete the Health apps declaration form on the App content page (Monitor & Improve >Policy > App content) in Play Console.
findings.implicationForProject: Host the privacy policy on a public HTTPS page in Arabic and English and link it from the Privacy Center screen. Request only the permissions the app needs and remove unused ones.

findings.requirement: Health Content and Services policy, part 2. Apps that are not regulated medical devices must carry a disclaimer in the store description: 'not a medical device and does not diagnose, treat, cure, or prevent any medical condition.' Apps must also remind users to consult a healthcare professional. Regulated medical-device apps must declare that status and provide proof on request.
findings.sourceQuote: Other health and medical apps must include a clear disclaimer in their app description indicating that the app is "not a medical device and does not diagnose, treat, cure, or prevent any medical condition." Apps must also remind users to consult a healthcare professional for medical advice, diagnosis, or treatment.
findings.implicationForProject: Add the exact disclaimer to the Play description (AR and EN). Show in-app reminders around the AI assistant and any wound-assessment output. Avoid diagnostic claims for AI features unless the product is regulated as a medical device.

findings.requirement: All apps on closed, open or production tracks must complete the Health apps declaration, even apps with no health features. Relevant medical categories include 'Healthcare Services and Management' (appointments, telehealth, health records, billing) and 'Diseases and Conditions Management' (which includes skin care). Selecting 'Medical Device Apps' triggers extra disclosures (EU MDR/IVDR for EEA users).
findings.sourceQuote: All developers that have an app published on Google Play must complete the Health apps declaration, including apps on closed testing, open testing, or production tracks.
findings.implicationForProject: Complete the declaration before the first closed-test release. Likely selections: Healthcare Services and Management, Diseases and Conditions Management, and possibly Clinical Decision Support if doctor-facing assessment tools exist. Do not select Medical Device unless it is regulated as one.

findings.requirement: CAMERA, ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION, ACCESS_COARSE_LOCATION, ACCESS_BACKGROUND_LOCATION, RECORD_AUDIO and calendar or SMS permissions count as health-sensitive under the Health apps policy. Apps using them must prominently disclose the use, describe the data, and obtain affirmative user consent.
findings.sourceQuote: If your app requires any of these permissions, it must prominently disclose how user data will be used, describe the type of data being accessed, and have the user provide affirmative consent for such use.
findings.implicationForProject: Before each runtime prompt for camera (wound photos), location (nurse matching) or microphone (calls), show an in-app disclosure and consent screen. Log the consent. Remove RECORD_AUDIO if it is not used (expo-image-picker adds it by default; set microphonePermission:false).

findings.requirement: Developers providing health apps (medical apps, human subjects research apps) must register a Play Console Organization account. Organization accounts require a D-U-N-S number that matches the Dun & Bradstreet profile.
findings.sourceQuote: When creating your Play Console account, developers providing the following services must register as an Organization: ... 1.2. Health apps, such as Medical apps and Human Subjects Research apps.
findings.implicationForProject: Publish under an Organization account for the Egyptian legal entity (Alia Group / operator), with a free D-U-N-S number, not a personal account. Account-type source: https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/13634885.

findings.requirement: Play Console Requirements policy, sections 3.3 and 3.4. Before submitting an app, provide an active demo account and sign-in details, and register app package names for Android developer verification. Since Sep 30, 2026, unregistered Play packages are removed.
findings.sourceQuote: Effective September 30, 2026, all Play packages must be registered to meet Android developer verification requirements.
findings.implicationForProject: Register the production and any variant package IDs in Play Console before uploading. Enter working review credentials for Patient, Doctor and Nurse roles in App access (Policy section 3.3, https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/10788890).

findings.requirement: Personal developer accounts created after November 13, 2023 must run a closed test with at least 12 testers opted in continuously for at least 14 days before they can apply for production access. Testers who opt out and back in must have 14 consecutive days.
findings.sourceQuote: Developers with personal accounts created after November 13, 2023, must run a closed test for their app with a minimum of 12 testers who have been opted in continuously for at least 14 days.
findings.implicationForProject: The page scopes this rule to personal accounts only. Because health apps must use an Organization account, the rule should not apply, but budget for it if a personal account is used by mistake. Production-access review usually takes up to 7 days.

findings.requirement: Apps that let users create an account must offer (1) a prominent in-app path to delete the account and associated data, and (2) a working web link where users can request deletion without reinstalling the app. Some data may be kept for security, fraud prevention or regulatory reasons if users are told. Healthcare apps may add extra flows to complete deletion.
findings.sourceQuote: provide users with an in-app path to delete their app accounts and associated data; and provide a web link resource where users can request app account deletion and associated data deletion.
findings.implicationForProject: Provide in-app deletion in Settings for all three roles, plus a public web deletion-request page naming 'Dress My Wound' or the developer name exactly as on Play. Enter that URL in the Data safety form. Explain any extra steps up front (cancel an active Play subscription, retain medical/payment records). Publish the retention periods for medical and financial records in the privacy policy. Ask processors (Paymob, AI vendor, storage) to delete user data as well.

findings.requirement: Data safety form: required for every app on closed, open or production tracks; internal-testing-only apps are exempt. It must cover data collected or shared by third-party SDKs, and needs a privacy policy. It includes the 'Health info' data type, an encryption-in-transit question, and a deletion-request question.
findings.sourceQuote: All developers that have an app published on Google Play must complete the Data safety form, including apps on closed, open, or production testing tracks.
findings.implicationForProject: Declare at least: Health info (wound records, symptoms), Photos, Location (approx/precise), Personal info (name, phone, email), Purchase history, App activity and Device IDs, including data from SDKs (analytics, crash reporting, AI provider, Paymob SDK if card data passes through it). Answer 'encrypted in transit' yes only if every SDK uses TLS.

findings.requirement: Photo and Video Permissions: apps targeting API 33+ may request READ_MEDIA_IMAGES or READ_MEDIA_VIDEO only when system pickers such as the Android Photo Picker are not enough for core functionality, typically gallery-type apps. Otherwise the permissions must be removed from the manifest. Custom pickers must still file a Play Console declaration. Full compliance has been mandatory since May 28, 2025.
findings.sourceQuote: Apps that target Android 13 or later (API level 33+) may only request the READ_MEDIA_IMAGES and READ_MEDIA_VIDEO permissions if system pickers (like the Android Photo Picker), are not sufficient for your app to provide core functionality.
findings.implicationForProject: Wound-photo upload should use the system photo picker or the camera (expo-image-picker / expo-camera). Block READ_MEDIA_IMAGES, READ_MEDIA_VIDEO and READ_MEDIA_VISUAL_USER_SELECTED via android.blockedPermissions in app config, then check the merged manifest of the AAB. The Expo SDK 57 image-picker docs list READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE as auto-added and do not document READ_MEDIA_* behavior. The same article adds a Contacts policy: apps targeting API 37+ may use READ_CONTACTS only with a declaration (mandatory 2027-01-27), so do not include READ_CONTACTS.

findings.requirement: Background location is allowed only when it is core to the app and gives significant user benefit. It needs Play Console approval: a Permissions Declaration Form naming one feature, a video of about 30 seconds or less, and a prominent in-app disclosure shown before the runtime prompt that uses the word 'location' and phrases like 'when the app is closed or not in use'. Foreground access is preferred. Location used only for ads or analytics is denied.
findings.sourceQuote: Your app should only request access to the location in the background if it's required for the core functionality of the app. ... apps that access location in the background must be approved via the permission declaration process in the developer console.
findings.implicationForProject: Keep isAndroidBackgroundLocationEnabled=false in the expo-location plugin (the SDK 57 default) and use foreground-only location for matching and address entry. If live nurse en-route tracking is needed, run it as a user-started foreground service with an FGS declaration rather than ACCESS_BACKGROUND_LOCATION. For API 37+ targets, one-time precise location (address pickers, search nearby) must use the location button; compliance is mandatory from 2027-01-27 (https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/17033915).

findings.requirement: Target audience and content: new apps and updates must declare a target age group. Including children brings the Families policy into play. Listings with child-appealing elements can be rejected if children are not targeted.
findings.sourceQuote: Any apps that include children in their target audience must comply with Google Play's Families Policy Requirements.
findings.implicationForProject: Declare 18+ only and avoid child-appealing store assets. Pediatric wound care should run through a guardian's account rather than child accounts. Including under-13 users would trigger Families policy obligations, including Families Self-Certified Ads SDKs only.

unresolved: Whether Silver/Gold/Platinum hybrid tiers count as 'more digital than physical'. Google gives no numeric test; only Play policy support can confirm that a tier sold mainly for real-world benefits (priority matching, reduced visit fees) may use Paymob.

Google Play Billing fee and lower service-fee terms for Egypt ('Rest of World') are not published yet. The page says 'Billing fee details for other regions are forthcoming'; the Rest of World rollout is 2027-09-30.
The 12-tester / 14-day page is scoped only to personal accounts created after 2023-11-13 and does not mention organization accounts. That organization accounts are exempt is an inference.
Expo SDK 57 expo-image-picker docs do not say whether the Android Photo Picker is the default or whether READ_MEDIA_IMAGES/VIDEO are merged into the manifest. Inspect the built AAB's merged manifest.

Whether the AI assistant or any wound-assessment feature is a regulated medical device under Egyptian Drug Authority rules (this decides the 'Medical Device Apps' declaration vs. the non-device disclaimer) was not checked against Egyptian sources.

The full User Data policy (answer 10144311) prominent-disclosure wording was not quoted directly. The disclosure and consent requirements here come from the Health app categories and background-location articles.
Whether priority matching (an in-app queue or ranking advantage) counts as digital or physical under Play's Payments policy is not addressed in any official source found.

research.topic: expo-sdk57: Expo SDK 57 platform defaults, app config (privacy manifests, blockedPermissions, edge-to-edge, predictive back), EAS build profiles and variants, expo-build-properties, and IAP library compatibility (expo-iap / react-native-iap / Play Billing), verified 2026-10-14

findings.requirement: Expo SDK 57 shipped on Jun 30, 2026. It moves React Native from 0.85 to 0.86 and keeps React at 19.2 (the versions table says React 19.2.3). It is the current stable SDK: npm dist-tags show latest = sdk-57 = expo@57.0.28 (published 2026-10-12), while next = 58.0.9 is the SDK 58 beta. Two regressions are fixed in later patches: the Hermes V1 memory regression in expo@57.0.9 (RN 0.86.2) and the dev startup-time regression in expo@57.0.17 (RN 0.86.3). In SDK 57, `expo prebuild` now clears and regenerates the android/ios folders by default.
findings.sourceQuote: SDK 57 upgrades React Native from 0.85 to 0.86. The React version is unchanged from SDK 56 — both SDK 56 and SDK 57 use React 19.2. ... expo@57.0.17 updates React Native to 0.86.3
findings.implicationForProject: apps/mobile/package.json already pins expo ~57.0.28, react-native 0.86.3 and react 19.2.3, which matches. Keep expo at 57.0.17 or later, because the Hermes V1 memory fix matters if reanimated or worklets are used. Treat android/ios as generated output (CNG), since prebuild now cleans them by default. Expo Go for SDK 57 is not in the stores, so testers need dev-client builds.

findings.requirement: The official SDK compatibility table lists SDK 57.0.0 as: React Native 0.86, React 19.2.3, minimum Node.js 22.13.x, Android 7+, compileSdkVersion 36, targetSdkVersion 36, iOS 16.4+, Xcode 26.4+. React Native 0.86 itself declares node engines "^20.19.4 || ^22.13.0 || ^24.3.0 || >= 25.0.0".
findings.sourceQuote: Expo SDK version Android version compileSdkVersion targetSdkVersion iOS version Xcode version 57.0.0 7+ 36 36 16.4+ 26.4+ ... 57.0.0 0.86 19.2.3 0.21.0 0.86-stable 22.13.x
findings.implicationForProject: eas.json base profile sets node 22.22.0, which satisfies the 22.13.x minimum. CI and local machines must use Node 22.13 or newer (or 24.3 or newer), not Node 20. iOS builds need Xcode 26.4 or newer. No compileSdk or targetSdk override is needed, because both default to 36.

findings.requirement: The Expo table gives the Android floor only as '7+'. The numeric defaults come from React Native 0.86's Gradle version catalog: minSdk 24, targetSdk 36, compileSdk 36, buildTools 36.0.0, NDK 27.1.12297006, AGP 8.12.0, Kotlin 2.1.20. The SDK 57 bare template's gradle.properties sets newArchEnabled=true, hermesEnabled=true and edgeToEdgeEnabled=true.
findings.sourceQuote:
minSdk = "24"
targetSdk = "36"
compileSdk = "36"
buildTools = "36.0.0"
ndkVersion = "27.1.12297006" ... agp = "8.12.0" ... kotlin = "2.1.20"
findings.implicationForProject: The Android app will support API 24 (Android 7.0) and up unless overridden through expo-build-properties android.minSdkVersion. If you set kotlinVersion explicitly, use 2.1.20, which is what OpenIAP also recommends for SDK 57. Do not force a newer Kotlin version.

findings.requirement: Google Play target API level rule: from August 31, 2026, new apps and app updates must target Android 16 (API 36) or higher. Existing apps must target API 35 or higher to stay available to new users on newer devices. An extension to November 1, 2026 can be requested.
findings.sourceQuote: Starting August 31, 2026: New apps and app updates must target Android 16 (API level 36) or higher to be submitted to Google Play
findings.implicationForProject: The SDK 57 default targetSdkVersion of 36 meets this. Do not lower targetSdkVersion through expo-build-properties, because Play would reject the AAB.

findings.requirement: SDK 56, which SDK 57 inherits, raised the minimum Xcode to 26.4 and the minimum iOS deployment target to 16.4. iOS 15.1 devices such as iPhone 7 and 6s are dropped. Apple separately requires that, since April 28, 2026, uploads to App Store Connect are built with Xcode 26 or later and an iOS 26 SDK.
findings.sourceQuote: Minimum Xcode bumped to 26.4. Minimum iOS / tvOS bumped to 16.4, macOS to 13.4. ... Upgrade Xcode if needed : Xcode 26.4 is required to compile a native iOS project.
findings.implicationForProject: The iOS app will support iOS 16.4 and later. Build with Xcode 26.4 to 26.6, which also meets Apple's iOS 26 SDK upload rule (https://developer.apple.com/news/upcoming-requirements/). Any local Expo modules need s.platforms ios '16.4' in their podspec.

findings.requirement: Xcode 27 / iOS 27 SDK: apps built with the iOS 27 SDK must use the UIKit scene-based life cycle, or they will not launch correctly on iOS 27. SDK 57 keeps the application-based life cycle by default. You can opt in with expo-build-properties ios.enableSceneSupport, which requires expo 57.0.23 or newer and the latest expo-build-properties. SDK 58 uses the scene life cycle by default.
findings.sourceQuote: SDK 57 apps keep the application-based life cycle by default. If you need to build with Xcode 27 and the iOS 27 SDK before upgrading to SDK 58, opt in with the ios.enableSceneSupport property of expo-build-properties ... expo@57.0.23 or newer.
findings.implicationForProject: Do not build the SDK 57 app with Xcode 27 unless expo-build-properties sets ios: { enableSceneSupport: true }. Without it, the app will black-screen on iOS 27. After enabling it, regression-test deep links and universal links (applinks) and push and URL handling.

findings.requirement: EAS Build image aliases. sdk-57 currently maps to macos-tahoe-26.5-xcode-26.6 (Xcode 26.6, Node 22.23.1) and ubuntu-26.04-jdk-17-ndk-r27b-sdk-57 (NDK 27.1.12297006, Node 22.23.1). The 'latest' alias moves with every new image release; Xcode 27.0 and 27.1 images already exist and are mapped to sdk-58. If eas.json has no image, the 'auto' alias picks one from the SDK and React Native version.
findings.sourceQuote: The latest alias will be updated with every new image release. ... Note: If you do not provide image in eas.json , your build by default will use the auto alias. ... macos-tahoe-26.5-xcode-26.6 ( latest , sdk-57 )
findings.implicationForProject: apps/mobile/eas.json sets android.image and ios.image to "latest". When Expo re-points 'latest' to an Xcode 27 image, iOS builds will silently use the iOS 27 SDK without scene support. Change both to "sdk-57", or remove the image field so 'auto' applies, for reproducible store builds.

findings.requirement: Google Play 16 KB page size: apps targeting Android 15 (API 35) or higher must support 16 KB memory page sizes on 64-bit devices. From February 1, 2027, app updates that do not support 16 KB cannot be released. NDK r28+ aligns to 16 KB by default; NDK r27 needs flexible-page-size flags. AGP 8.5.1 or newer handles APK zip alignment. React Native 0.77+ supports 16 KB, and Expo added -DANDROID_SUPPORT_FLEXIBLE_PAGE_SIZES=ON for NDK r27 to its native packages (PR #37446, June 2025, SDK 53).
findings.effectiveDate: 2027-02-01 (update block); already required for API 35+ targets
findings.sourceQuote: all apps targeting Android 15 (API level 35) and higher must support 16 KB memory page sizes on 64-bit devices on Google Play. Starting February 1, 2027, if your app updates don't support 16 KB memory page sizes, you won't be able to release these updates.
findings.implicationForProject: The SDK 57 toolchain (RN 0.86, NDK r27 with Expo and RN flexible-page flags, AGP 8.12) is expected to be compliant. However, Expo docs do not explicitly certify SDK 57, so verify each production AAB in the Play Console App bundle explorer or with `zipalign -c -P 16`. Check every third-party .so you add (Paymob native SDKs, IAP, image libraries). Confidence is 'official-but-ambiguous' because the Google rule is official but Expo SDK 57 compliance is inferred from React Native and Expo engineering sources (https://reactnative.dev/blog/2025/01/21/version-0.77, https://github.com/expo/expo/pull/37446).

findings.requirement: Edge-to-edge is always on and cannot be disabled from SDK 54 onward, because apps target Android 16. SDK 55 removed `edgeToEdgeEnabled` from app.json. The expo-status-bar backgroundColor and translucent props and most expo-navigation-bar color and behavior APIs became deprecated no-ops. React Native 0.86 in SDK 57 adds edge-to-edge fixes.
findings.sourceQuote: With Expo SDK 54 and React Native 0.81 now targeting Android 16, edge-to-edge will be enabled in all Android apps, and cannot be disabled . (SDK 55: "edgeToEdgeEnabled removed from app.json config : edge-to-edge is now mandatory when targeting Android 16+.")
findings.implicationForProject: Do not add android.edgeToEdgeEnabled, androidStatusBar.backgroundColor or androidNavigationBar config, since they are removed or no-ops. Every screen, especially the checkout, booking and emergency banners, must handle insets with react-native-safe-area-context or the router's safe-area handling. QA should check RTL Arabic layouts under system bars and with gesture navigation.

findings.requirement: `android.predictiveBackGestureEnabled` is a boolean app config key that enables the predictive back gesture on Android 13 (API 33) and later. It defaults to false; the v57.0.0 app config reference is identical to latest. It maps to android:enableOnBackInvokedCallback.
findings.sourceQuote: predictiveBackGestureEnabled Type: boolean • Path: android . predictiveBackGestureEnabled Enable your app to use the predictive back gesture on Android 13 (API level 33) and later. Default to false.
findings.implicationForProject: app.config.ts opts in with predictiveBackGestureEnabled: true. That is allowed, but it departs from the SDK 57 default. Test all hardware-back flows on Android 13 and later: modals, the Paymob payment WebView or redirect, multi-step booking and the unsaved-form guards. If any flow relies on intercepting back, either verify it or set the flag to false. SDK 56 notes say predictive back support in the native stack (Stack v5) was still experimental.

findings.requirement: iOS privacy manifests are declared through `ios.privacyManifests` in app config, which generates PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy at prebuild. Supported keys are NSPrivacyAccessedAPITypes (with NSPrivacyAccessedAPIType and NSPrivacyAccessedAPITypeReasons), NSPrivacyTracking, NSPrivacyTrackingDomains and NSPrivacyCollectedDataTypes (with Type, Linked, Tracking and Purposes). Expo warns that Apple does not correctly parse every PrivacyInfo file from static CocoaPods. The SDK 57 template Podfile aggregates pod privacy manifests by default (privacy_file_aggregation_enabled unless apple.privacyManifestAggregationEnabled is 'false'); this is controlled by expo-build-properties ios.privacyManifestAggregationEnabled.
findings.sourceQuote: You can include an iOS privacy manifest by using the privacyManifests field under expo.ios in your app config. ... As of now, Apple does not correctly parse all the PrivacyInfo files included by static CocoaPods dependencies ... You may need to include the required reasons for the APIs used by those dependencies in your app's PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy file or the configuration in the app.json .
findings.implicationForProject: app.config.ts already declares UserDefaults CA92.1, FileTimestamp C617.1, SystemBootTime 35F9.1, DiskSpace E174.1 and the collected data types. Keep aggregation on, meaning do not set privacyManifestAggregationEnabled to false. After adding expo-iap or Paymob SDKs, re-check node_modules/*/ios/PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy and merge their reasons. Upload to TestFlight to get Apple's missing-reason email before submission. Template Podfile: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/expo/expo/sdk-57/templates/expo-template-bare-minimum/ios/Podfile.

findings.requirement: `ios.deploymentTarget` is a built-in app config property on SDK 56 and later, with MAJOR.MINOR format. expo-build-properties' ios.deploymentTarget is deprecated. The SDK 57 template Podfile falls back to '16.4'.
findings.sourceQuote: deploymentTarget (optional) string Deprecated: use built-in ios.deploymentTarget property instead (SDK 56 and greater).
findings.implicationForProject: If you raise the iOS minimum, set ios.deploymentTarget in app.config.ts, not in expo-build-properties. Leaving it unset gives 16.4, which matches expo-iap's validated setup.

findings.requirement: `android.blockedPermissions` lists permissions to remove from the final merged AndroidManifest.xml using tools:node="remove". It is the only way to strip permissions that library manifests add, and it is not available in Expo Go. `android.permissions` only adds permissions.
findings.sourceQuote: The only way to remove permissions that are added by package-level AndroidManifest.xml files is to block them with the android.blockedPermissions property.
findings.implicationForProject: The current blockedPermissions list (location, camera, audio, storage, media, contacts, phone state, AD_ID) is valid. Never add com.android.vending.BILLING to it: expo-iap's own manifest declares that permission, and Play Billing needs it. Remove CAMERA and READ_MEDIA_* from the list when the wound-photo feature ships. Otherwise the runtime request silently fails.

findings.requirement: expo-build-properties (sdk-57 tag 57.0.22) configures android/gradle.properties and ios/Podfile.properties.json during prebuild. Android options include compileSdkVersion, targetSdkVersion, minSdkVersion, buildToolsVersion, kotlinVersion, buildArchs, enableMinifyInReleaseBuilds (R8), enableShrinkResourcesInReleaseBuilds, usesCleartextTraffic (platform default false on Android 9+), useLegacyPackaging (default false) and extraProguardRules. iOS options include enableSceneSupport, privacyManifestAggregationEnabled, useFrameworks and usePrecompiledModules (default true). Shared options include useHermesV1 (default true) and buildReactNativeFromSource (default false). The SDK 58 beta turns R8 on by default.
findings.sourceQuote: This config plugin configures how Prebuild command generates the native android and ios directories and therefore cannot be used with projects that don't run npx expo prebuild (bare projects).
findings.implicationForProject: Add the expo-build-properties plugin for: (1) ios.enableSceneSupport if Xcode 27 is ever used on SDK 57; (2) android.enableMinifyInReleaseBuilds and enableShrinkResourcesInReleaseBuilds to prepare for SDK 58's R8 default, with keep rules tested for IAP and Paymob; (3) an explicit kotlinVersion of 2.1.20 only if needed. Do not override compileSdk or targetSdk; 36 is correct.

findings.requirement: eas.json best practice. The default profiles are development (developmentClient: true, distribution: internal), preview (distribution: internal) and production ({}). `distribution` is store or internal, and internal needs an .apk or .ipa. Android `buildType` is app-bundle (:app:bundleRelease, .aab) or apk (:app:assembleRelease); .apk is recommended for preview and .aab for Google Play. `cli.appVersionSource: "remote"` has been recommended since EAS CLI 12.0.0, combined with `autoIncrement: true` on production. With remote versioning, the versionCode and buildNumber in app config are ignored. `environment` (development, preview or production) selects EAS environment variables.
findings.sourceQuote: The remote version source is the recommended behavior from EAS CLI version 12.0.0 . EAS servers can store and manage your app's developer-facing build version ( android.versionCode and ios.buildNumber ) remotely. To enable it, you need to set cli.appVersionSource to remote in eas.json . Then, under the production build profile, you can set the autoIncrement property to true .
findings.implicationForProject: apps/mobile/eas.json follows this. It has cli.appVersionSource remote, internal development and preview APK profiles, store and app-bundle profiles for preview-store and production with autoIncrement, and per-profile environment. Do not put versionCode or buildNumber in app.config.ts (it already relies on remote). Use `eas build:version:sync` before local native builds. Related references: https://docs.expo.dev/eas/json/ and https://docs.expo.dev/build/eas-json/.

findings.requirement: App variants pattern: set APP_VARIANT in each eas.json profile's env and read it in app.config to switch name, android.package and ios.bundleIdentifier. In Expo's example, an unset APP_VARIANT means the production variant. Switching variants locally needs `prebuild --clean`. Services that register the app ID (FCM, Maps and so on) need a separate configuration per variant.
findings.sourceQuote: When you run eas build --profile production the APP_VARIANT variable environment is not set, and the build runs as the production variant. ... APP_VARIANT changes only the app's name and package name on Android and bundle identifier on iOS. It does not affect how the binary is compiled.
findings.implicationForProject: app.config.ts defaults to 'development' when APP_VARIANT is unset, which is the opposite of Expo's example. That is safe only because every eas.json profile sets APP_VARIANT. Make sure `eas update`, `eas submit`, `expo config` and CI scripts also set APP_VARIANT=production, or they will resolve the dev identifiers. My inference, not stated in the Expo doc: store IAP products are tied to the production package and bundle ID, so purchase testing needs the production identifiers, typically via preview-store or a TestFlight / internal track build.

findings.requirement: Architecture and engine. The Legacy Architecture was dropped in SDK 55 and `newArchEnabled` was removed from app.json. Hermes V1 is the default engine from SDK 56 (React Native 0.84+). Opting out with useHermesV1: false also requires buildReactNativeFromSource: true.
findings.sourceQuote: you will not be able to use the Legacy Architecture in SDK 55 projects and later. Accordingly, the newArchEnabled config option has been removed from app.json .
findings.implicationForProject: Every native dependency, including any Paymob React Native SDK wrapper, IAP library and maps or camera modules, must work on the New Architecture (Fabric/TurboModules, or the interop layer). Check this before adoption, and do not add newArchEnabled to app config.

findings.requirement: SDK 58 status: a beta has been out since Sep 15, 2026 with React Native 0.88 RC; stable ships after React Native 0.88. It is not stable as of 2026-10-14 (npm latest is still 57.0.28). Notable SDK 58 breaking changes: (1) the scene life cycle; (2) R8 on by default in release builds; (3) Node 22.13+, 24.3+ or 26+ required; (4) on iOS, expo-localization no longer force-enables RTL from the device locale with supportsRTL, and layout direction follows I18nManager; (5) React Native Strict TypeScript API by default.
findings.sourceQuote: expo-localization : on iOS, RTL is no longer force-enabled from the device locale with supportsRTL ; layout direction follows I18nManager ( #48086 ).
findings.implicationForProject: Stay on SDK 57 for the first release. For the Arabic (غير لي) UI, drive RTL explicitly through I18nManager.allowRTL and forceRTL plus a reload, and do not rely on expo-localization supportsRTL auto-forcing. That keeps the app correct on SDK 58. Also avoid react-native/Libraries/* deep imports now.

findings.requirement: In-app purchases with Expo need a development build because they are not available in Expo Go. Expo's IAP guide lists two libraries: react-native-purchases (RevenueCat) and expo-iap (OpenIAP).
findings.sourceQuote: In-app purchase libraries require configuring custom native code. Native code is not configurable when using Expo Go. Instead, create a development build
findings.implicationForProject: Silver, Gold and Platinum digital entitlements such as the AI assistant must be tested in dev-client or preview-store builds on physical devices. The Expo docs do not list react-native-iap.

findings.requirement: expo-iap: latest is 6.0.2 (npm, published 2026-10-14T01:32Z). 6.0.0 was published 2026-10-09 and is a new major release. Peer dependencies are expo, react and react-native at '*' plus optional Amazon Kepler packages. The library's documented baseline is Expo SDK 53+, with SDK 57 / React Native 0.86 as the validated baseline, Kotlin 2.1.20, iOS 16.4+, Android minSdk 23+ and compileSdk 36+. openiap-versions.json pins google 4.0.2 and apple 4.0.2. The Maven POM for io.github.hyochan.openiap:openiap-google:4.0.2 depends on com.android.billingclient:billing 9.1.0, and iOS uses StoreKit 2. The package manifest declares com.android.vending.BILLING.
findings.sourceQuote: Expo SDK 53+; SDK 57 / React Native 0.86 is the validated baseline ... expo-iap uses OpenIAP Android artifacts backed by Google Play Billing Library v 9.1.0 . ... Expo SDK 57: use Kotlin 2.1.20
findings.implicationForProject: expo-iap is the recommended IAP library for this Expo app if store billing is implemented directly without RevenueCat. Pin the exact version (6.0.2), because 6.0.0 is days old and carries breaking changes in restore and offer-code behavior. Add the "expo-iap" config plugin. Use it only for digital subscription entitlements; TetraSol physical goods and in-person services stay on Paymob. Other sources: https://www.npmjs.com/package/expo-iap and https://repo1.maven.org/maven2/io/github/hyochan/openiap/openiap-google/4.0.2/openiap-google-4.0.2.pom.

findings.requirement: react-native-iap: latest is 17.0.2 (npm, published 2026-10-14T01:11Z; 17.0.0 on 2026-10-09). Peer dependencies are react and react-native at '*', react-native-nitro-modules >=0.36.5 (latest 0.37.1) and optional Amazon packages. It uses the same OpenIAP 4.0.2 artifacts, so Play Billing 9.1.0 and StoreKit 2. The official docs say v15+ is for bare React Native CLI projects only, that Expo support ended in v15.0.0, and that it requires React Native 0.79+ and iOS 15.0+.
findings.sourceQuote: react-native-iap v15+ is for bare React Native CLI projects only and requires React Native 0.79+ (Nitro Modules), iOS 15.0+ (StoreKit 2), and Android minSdkVersion 23 + with compileSdkVersion 36 + . Expo support ended in v15.0.0 — use expo-iap instead; it provides the same API on Expo Modules.
findings.implicationForProject: Do not add react-native-iap to this Expo SDK 57 app. It ships no Expo config plugin and the maintainers direct Expo users to expo-iap. Package page: https://www.npmjs.com/package/react-native-iap.

findings.requirement: Google Play Billing Library deprecation schedule (new apps and updates deadline, then extension deadline): v7 Aug 31, 2026 (extension Nov 1, 2026); v8 Aug 31, 2027 (Nov 1, 2027); v9 Aug 31, 2028 (Nov 1, 2028). PBL 9.0.0 was released 2026-05-19 and 9.1.0 on 2026-06-18. The page notes that the com.google.android.play.billingclient.version manifest entry must survive manifest merging.
findings.sourceQuote: Reminder: By Aug 31, 2026, all new apps and updates to existing apps must use Billing Library version 8 or later. If you need more time to update your app, you can request an extension until Nov 1, 2026.
findings.implicationForProject: expo-iap 6.0.2 (PBL 9.1.0) is compliant until Aug 31, 2028.
