research.topic: store-listing: App Store Connect and Google Play listing metadata limits, assets, age/content ratings, review access, categories, privacy policy URL, and Arabic localization of the app name (verified 2026-10-14)

findings.requirement: Apple app name: 2 to 30 characters. Required and localizable (App Information). Editable only until you submit to App Review, then only when you create a new version.
findings.sourceQuote: The name must be at least two characters and no more than 30 characters. You can edit it until you submit the app to App Review.
findings.implicationForProject: 'Dress My Wound' is 14 characters and 'غير لي' is 6, so both fit. Lock the names before the first submission, because changing them later needs a new version. Set the Arabic name in the Arabic localization under App Information.

findings.requirement: Apple subtitle: up to 30 characters. Optional and localizable. Must follow the metadata rules: no prices, no references to other apps, no unverifiable product claims.
findings.sourceQuote: A summary of your app that appears under your app's name on your App Store product page. This can't be longer than 30 characters.
findings.implicationForProject: Write a separate English (U.K.) subtitle and Arabic subtitle, each 30 characters or fewer. Do not use clinical-efficacy claims such as 'heals wounds faster' (Guideline 2.3.7: unverifiable claims).

findings.requirement: Apple promotional text: up to 170 characters. Can be changed without submitting a new version.
findings.sourceQuote: This property can't be longer than 170 characters.
findings.implicationForProject: Use this field for time-sensitive messages, such as TetraSol availability or tier launches, so the description stays stable. Still no prices or claims that cannot be verified.

findings.requirement: Apple description: up to 4000 characters, plain text only (no HTML). Required and localizable.
findings.sourceQuote: Limited to 4000 characters. The description should be in plain text, with line breaks as needed. HTML format isn't supported.
findings.implicationForProject: Write separate English and Arabic descriptions, each 4000 characters or fewer, with no markup. Guideline 2.3.2 requires the description to say clearly that Silver, Gold and Platinum need an additional purchase. Guideline 1.4.1 says to remind users to check with a doctor.

findings.requirement: Apple keywords: up to 100 bytes. Each keyword must be longer than two characters. Required and localizable. Do not repeat the app name or company name, and do not use other apps' or companies' names.
findings.sourceQuote: One or more keywords (each greater than two characters) describing your app. You can provide up to 100 bytes of content... Names of other apps or companies aren't allowed.
findings.implicationForProject: The limit is in bytes, not characters. Arabic letters take 2 bytes each in UTF-8, so the Arabic keyword set holds roughly 50 Arabic characters (this is an inference about encoding). Keep 'TetraSol', 'Dress My Wound' and 'غير لي' out of the keywords because the name and company are already indexed. Never use competitor names.

findings.requirement: Apple 'What's New in This Version': up to 4000 characters. Not available for the first version and required for every later version. Guideline 2.3.12 requires significant changes to be listed specifically.
findings.sourceQuote: This property isn't available for the first version of the app but required for all subsequent versions.
findings.implicationForProject: Prepare per-release notes in English and Arabic from version 1.0.1 onward. Generic text such as 'bug fixes' is only acceptable for minor releases.

findings.requirement: Apple Support URL: required and localizable. It must lead to actual contact information (legal address, email address, telephone number) as local law may require. Give the full URL including the protocol.
findings.sourceQuote: This URL must lead to actual contact information (legal address, email address, telephone number), as may be required by local law
findings.implicationForProject: Publish a live support page, in English and Arabic, with the Egyptian legal entity's address, a support email and a phone number in +20 format. Placeholder or empty sites are rejected under Guideline 2.1(a).

findings.requirement: Apple Privacy Policy URL: required for iOS and localizable. Privacy Choices URL is optional and localizable. Guideline 5.1.1(i) requires the policy link both in the App Store Connect metadata and inside the app. The policy must cover what data is collected and how it is used, how third parties protect it, retention and deletion, and how users revoke consent or request deletion.
findings.sourceQuote: All apps must include a link to their privacy policy in the App Store Connect metadata field and within the app in an easily accessible manner.
findings.implicationForProject: Host Arabic and English privacy policies at stable HTTPS URLs and enter a per-locale URL. The policy must name Paymob, the AI provider and analytics SDKs as recipients, cover retention of health and wound-photo data, and explain the account deletion path. Link it from the in-app Privacy Center.

findings.requirement: Apple's updated age rating system added 13+, 16+ and 18+ to the existing 4+ and 9+. It added required questions on in-app controls, capabilities, medical or wellness topics and violent themes. The deadline to answer was January 31, 2026, after which updates are interrupted. Social media capability questions were added on July 9, 2026.
findings.sourceQuote: Please provide responses to the updated age rating questions for each of your apps by January 31, 2026, to avoid an interruption when submitting your app updates in App Store Connect.
findings.effectiveDate: 2025-07-24 announced; 2026-01-31 response deadline (passed); 2026-07-09 social media questions added
findings.implicationForProject: The new app must complete the full current questionnaire, including the In-App Controls, Capabilities (Messaging and Chat for patient-clinician chat; Social Media only if there is a feed), and Medical or Wellness sections, before the first submission.

findings.requirement: Apple age-rating mapping (iOS 26 and later): Health and wellness topics gives 9+. Infrequent medical or treatment information gives 13+. Frequent medical or treatment information gives 16+. User-generated content, Messaging and chat, and Advertising sit at the 4+ level. Unrestricted web access gives 16+. Guideline 2.3.6 requires honest answers.
findings.sourceQuote: 16+ ... Capabilities: Unrestricted web access Medical or Wellness: Frequent medical or treatment information
findings.implicationForProject: A wound-care app that gives treatment guidance, nurse care plans and an AI assistant will probably have to answer 'Frequent' for Medical or Treatment Information, which gives a 16+ global rating. Plan the target audience and marketing for 16+. Do not under-rate. Keep the Paymob web checkout limited to its own domain so it does not count as 'Unrestricted web access'.

findings.requirement: Apple 'Regulated Medical Devices' declaration: required for apps available in the EU/EEA, UK or U.S. that have Health & Fitness or Medical as primary or secondary category, or that list 'frequent' Medical or Treatment information in the age rating.
findings.sourceQuote: Apps that are available in the EU/EEA, UK, or U.S., and have a primary or secondary category of Health & Fitness or Medical, or that have "frequent" Medical or Treatment information listed in the age rating, are required to complete this declaration.
findings.implicationForProject: If distribution is limited to Egypt, the declaration is not triggered. Any later expansion to the EU, UK or US will trigger it, because the app will be in the Medical category with frequent treatment information. Keep availability set to Egypt only until a regulatory assessment is done.

findings.requirement: Apple category definitions. Medical: 'Apps that are focused on medical education, information management, or health reference for patients or healthcare professionals.' Health & Fitness: 'Apps related to healthy living, including stress management, fitness, and recreational activities.' Primary category is required; secondary is optional. Guideline 2.3.5 lets Apple change a category that is 'way off base'.
findings.sourceQuote: Medical Apps that are focused on medical education, information management, or health reference for patients or healthcare professionals.
findings.implicationForProject: Recommend Medical as the primary category: wound care, nurse/doctor matching and medical record-keeping fit that definition better than fitness. Shopping or Health & Fitness are optional secondary categories. Either health category triggers the medical-device declaration if the app is later sold in the EU, UK or US.

findings.requirement: Apple App Review Information. If the app requires login, give a demo username and password that must not expire, and put additional accounts in Notes. Notes can hold up to 4000 bytes, in any language. The contact phone must be in international format (for example +852), not digits only. Guideline 2.1(a) requires demo account details and a live backend. A built-in demo mode is allowed only with Apple's prior approval.
findings.sourceQuote: The demo account is used during the App Review process and must not expire. Details for additional accounts should be included in the Notes field.
findings.effectiveDate: International phone format requirement added to the docs 2026-08-19
findings.implicationForProject: Create permanent reviewer accounts for Patient, Doctor and Nurse that skip OTP or use a static OTP. Put the patient account in the username/password fields and the doctor and nurse accounts in Notes, with step-by-step test paths. Enter the contact phone as +20…. Keep the staging or production backend and Paymob sandbox running during review.

findings.requirement: Apple screenshots: 1 to 10 per device size, in .jpeg, .jpg or .png, with no alpha channel or transparency. The required size listed is 'iPhone with Dynamic Island (medium display)' (1179x2556 or 1206x2622 portrait), plus iPad 13-inch (2064x2752 or 2048x2732) if the app supports iPadOS. The 'Face ID (large display)' row (1284x2778 / 1242x2688) still says it is required when large Dynamic Island screenshots (1260x2736 / 1290x2796 / 1320x2868) are not provided.
findings.sourceQuote: iPhone: At least one screenshot for iPhone with Dynamic Island (medium display). iPad (if your app supports iPadOS): At least one screenshot for iPad 13-inch display.
findings.effectiveDate: No-alpha rule added to the docs 2026-07-08
findings.implicationForProject: Because the page is internally inconsistent, upload two iPhone sets per locale: 1320x2868 for the large display and 1206x2622 for the medium display. Export as flattened PNG or JPEG with no alpha. Set ios.supportsTablet=false in the app config unless you will also produce 13-inch iPad screenshots (2064x2752). Produce English and Arabic (right-to-left) sets.

findings.requirement: iPhone Duo screenshots: starting in April 2027, they are required for any app built with the iOS 27.1 SDK or later. Sizes are 1398x2034 for the outer display and 2007x2853 for the inner display (portrait).
findings.sourceQuote: Starting in April 2027, screenshots will be required for any app using the iOS 27.1 SDK or later.
findings.implicationForProject: Not needed for the current Expo SDK 57 submission unless the EAS build image uses the iOS 27.1 SDK. Add iPhone Duo screenshot generation to the release checklist before April 2027.

findings.requirement: Apple metadata content rules. 2.3.3: screenshots must show the app in use, not only a splash or login screen. 2.3.7: no prices in name, subtitle or screenshots, and no keyword stuffing. 2.3.8: metadata and screenshots must be appropriate for a 4+ audience even if the app is rated higher. 2.3.2: state clearly which features need an additional purchase. 2.3.9: use fictional account data in screenshots.
findings.sourceQuote: Metadata should be appropriate for all audiences, so make sure your app and in-app purchase icons, screenshots, and previews adhere to a 4+ age rating even if your app is rated higher.
findings.implicationForProject: Screenshots must not show graphic wound photos; use illustrated or neutral imagery and fictional patient data. Do not show EGP prices in screenshots or subtitle. Label subscription tiers as requiring purchase. Do not imply AI diagnosis.

findings.requirement: Guideline 1.4.1: medical apps that could give inaccurate data, or could be used to diagnose or treat patients, may be reviewed with greater scrutiny. They should remind users to check with a doctor, and should submit a link to any regulatory clearance.
findings.sourceQuote: Apps should remind users to check with a doctor in addition to using the app and before making medical decisions.
findings.implicationForProject: Put the 'consult your doctor / not a diagnosis' disclaimer in the description and in the AI assistant UI. Explain in the App Review Notes that the AI is informational only and how clinicians are verified.

findings.requirement: Apple localization for Egypt: the Egypt storefront's default language is English (U.K.), with Arabic and French as additional languages. The app name and privacy policy URL are localized under App Information; description and keywords are localized per version. Locales without metadata fall back to the next most relevant localization, then to the primary language.
findings.sourceQuote: EGY | Egypt | English (U.K.) | Arabic, French
findings.implicationForProject: Provide two complete localizations: English (U.K.) with name 'Dress My Wound' and Arabic with name 'غير لي', each with its own subtitle, keywords, description, privacy URL and screenshots. Using English (U.K.) rather than English (U.S.) as primary or as an added locale matches Egypt's default storefront language.

findings.requirement: Apple localization mechanics: a new language's screenshots and properties default to the primary language's, except description and keywords. The app name and privacy policy URL for each language are entered under App Information. Name, Subtitle, Privacy Policy URL, Support URL and What's New are marked Localized.
findings.sourceQuote: When you add a language to your app, screenshots and the properties for the new language default to those of the primary language, except for the description and keywords.
findings.implicationForProject: After adding Arabic, explicitly replace the inherited English screenshots with Arabic right-to-left screenshots, and set the Arabic name 'غير لي' under App Information > Arabic.

findings.requirement: Google Play listing limits: app name 30 characters (one localized name per language), short description 80 characters, full description 4000 characters. The limits apply equally to full-width and half-width characters.
findings.sourceQuote: App name ... 30 character limit ... You can add one localized name per language. ... Short description ... 80 character limit ... Full description ... 4000 character limit
findings.implicationForProject: Add an Arabic ('ar') translation with title 'غير لي' and English (en-GB or en-US) with title 'Dress My Wound'. Keep the Arabic short description to 80 characters or fewer and the full description to 4000 or fewer.

findings.requirement: Google Play metadata policy: title 30 characters or fewer. No emojis, emoticons or repeated special characters in title, icon or developer name. No ALL CAPS unless part of the brand. No text implying ranking, price, promotions or Google Play programs. No unattributed or anonymous testimonials in the description.
findings.sourceQuote: Your app title must be 30 characters or less. Don't use text or image in the app title, icon, or developer name that indicate store performance or ranking, price or promotional information
findings.implicationForProject: Do not write 'DRESS MY WOUND' in all caps unless that is the registered brand style. Do not put 'Free' or tier prices in the title or icon. Remove any patient testimonials from the description unless they are attributed.

findings.requirement: Google Play short description: required. Avoid 'Best', '#1', 'Top', 'New', 'Discount', 'Sale', calls to action ('download now'), keyword stuffing, emojis, line breaks, repeated punctuation and symbols.
findings.sourceQuote: You must provide a short description to publish your store listing. ... 80 character limit
findings.implicationForProject: Write plain, factual Arabic and English one-liners, for example wound-care follow-up with licensed nurses and doctors, with no emojis and no CTA.

findings.requirement: Google Play app icon: required. 32-bit PNG with alpha, 512x512 px, sRGB, max 1024KB, full square. Google Play applies masking with a corner radius of 30% of icon size, and applies shadows itself.
findings.sourceQuote: Final size: 512px x 512px; Format: 32-bit PNG; Color space: sRGB; Max file size: 1024KB; Shape: Full square – Google Play dynamically handles masking.
findings.implicationForProject: Export a separate 512x512 full-square store icon without pre-rounded corners or drop shadow. This is different from the adaptive launcher icon in the Expo app config. No badges or text.

findings.requirement: Google Play feature graphic: required to publish. JPEG or 24-bit PNG with no alpha, 1024x500 px. Keep key elements away from the cut-off zones, and avoid words such as 'Best', 'Free' or 'New'.
findings.sourceQuote: You must provide a feature graphic to publish your store listing. ... JPEG or 24-bit PNG (no alpha) Dimensions: 1024px by 500px
findings.implicationForProject: Produce localized English and Arabic 1024x500 graphics with no alpha channel and the brand centered. The Arabic version should be laid out right to left.

findings.requirement: Google Play screenshots. At least 2 are required to publish (the page says 'across different device types'), with up to 8 per device type. Format JPEG or 24-bit PNG with no alpha. Minimum dimension 320 px, maximum 3840 px, and the long side can be at most twice the short side. To be eligible for recommendation formats, apps need at least 4 screenshots at 1080 px or more, portrait 9:16 (minimum 1080x1920). Tablet and Chromebook screenshots: minimum 4, 1080–7680 px, 16:9 or 9:16.
findings.sourceQuote: Minimum dimension: 320px Maximum dimension: 3840px The maximum dimension of your screenshot can't be more than twice as long as the minimum dimension.
findings.implicationForProject: Produce 4 to 8 phone screenshots per locale at 1080x1920 (9:16), flattened with no alpha. Note that modern 19.5:9 raw captures (for example 1080x2400) exceed the 2:1 ratio rule and must be cropped or padded to 9:16. Add alt text for each screenshot.

findings.requirement: Google Play preview video: optional, one YouTube URL. Must be public or unlisted, with ads/monetization off, not age-restricted, and embeddable.
findings.sourceQuote: You can add one preview video to your store listing by entering a YouTube URL in the "preview video" field.
findings.implicationForProject: Optional. If used, show actual app UI in the first 10 seconds, localize it, and avoid graphic wound imagery.

findings.requirement: Google Play content rating: the IARC questionnaire (Policy > App content) is required for new apps and for updates that change answers. Ratings come from regional authorities. PEGI covers the listed European and Middle East countries, which include the UAE and Turkey but not Egypt. 'IARC Generic' ratings (3+, 7+, 12+, 16+, 18+) apply in areas without a participating authority.
findings.sourceQuote: In countries and territories that aren't represented by a participating rating authority, a separate rating will suggest the age appropriateness of an app or game. IARC Generic
findings.implicationForProject: Egypt is absent from every listed authority, so the IARC Generic rating presumably applies there (an inference). Complete the questionnaire accurately, including chat between users, sharing of user-generated photos, and digital purchases. Redo it if AI chat or community features change.

findings.requirement: Google Play target audience: you must declare the target age group. Before completing 'Target audience and content' you must have declared ads, provided app access instructions, and added a privacy policy. Apps whose audience includes children must follow the Families policy.
findings.sourceQuote: Before filling out the "Target audience and content" section, you must have declared whether or not your app contains ads and provided instructions for app access . You must also add a privacy policy .
findings.implicationForProject: Declare 18+, or 16+ to match the Apple rating, as the target audience to stay out of Families policy scope. Minors can be managed through guardian accounts rather than by targeting children.

findings.requirement: Google Play categories. Medical: 'Drug and clinical references, calculators, handbooks for healthcare providers, medical journals and news'. Health and Fitness: 'Personal fitness, workout tracking, diet and nutritional tips, health and safety'. Up to 5 tags. Category and tags are set under Store settings.
findings.sourceQuote: Medical Drug and clinical references, calculators, handbooks for healthcare providers, medical journals and news
findings.implicationForProject: Choose Medical. Google's health-app guidance names telehealth, patient portals and disease management as medical apps. Pick up to 5 relevant tags.

findings.requirement: Google Play contact details: a support email is required. Phone and website are optional but recommended. All three are shown publicly on the listing.
findings.sourceQuote: A contact email address is required, but to provide your users with the best support experience, we also highly recommend including a website where users can contact you.
findings.implicationForProject: Use a monitored role mailbox (for example support@ on the company domain), the +20 support phone and the same support URL used for Apple.

findings.requirement: Google Play privacy policy: a link is required in the Play Console field and inside the app. It must be on an active, publicly accessible, non-geofenced URL (no PDFs), must not be editable, must be labelled as a privacy policy, and must name the listed developer entity or the app. Account deletion must remove the associated data.
findings.sourceQuote: Please make sure your privacy policy is available on an active, publicly accessible and non-geofenced URL (no PDFs) and is non-editable.
findings.implicationForProject: Host the policy as an HTML page that is not geo-blocked outside Egypt, so reviewers can reach it. Name the developer entity shown on Play. Keep it consistent with the Data safety form.

findings.requirement: Google Play Health apps declaration: every developer with an app on any track (including closed or open testing) must complete it under Policy > App content and pick the health features offered. Options include Healthcare Services and Management, Diseases and Conditions Management (covers skin care), and Medication and Treatment Management.
findings.sourceQuote: All developers that have an app published on Google Play must complete the Health apps declaration, including apps on closed testing, open testing, or production tracks.
findings.implicationForProject: Declare at least Healthcare Services and Management, Diseases and Conditions Management and Medication and Treatment Management. Do not select Medical Device Apps unless the app is regulated as a device.

findings.requirement: Google Play Health Content and Services policy: health and medical apps that are not regulated medical devices must state in the app description that the app is 'not a medical device and does not diagnose, treat, cure, or prevent any medical condition', and must remind users to consult a healthcare professional.
findings.sourceQuote: Other health and medical apps must include a clear disclaimer in their app description indicating that the app is "not a medical device and does not diagnose, treat, cure, or prevent any medical condition."
findings.implicationForProject: Add this disclaimer word for word in English, plus a faithful Arabic translation, in the Play full description. Mirror it in the Apple description and inside the app, including the AI assistant.

findings.requirement: Google Play sign-in details (app access): if any part of the app is behind login or membership, you must give reviewers everything needed to get in. Up to five sets of instructions are allowed. Use 'Any other instructions' to explain one-time passwords or MFA.
findings.sourceQuote: If your entire app or parts of your app are restricted based on login credentials, sign in details, memberships, location, or other forms of authentication, you must provide all required details to enable access to your app .
findings.implicationForProject: Provide separate instruction sets for Patient, Doctor, Nurse and a Gold or Platinum subscriber (4 of the 5 allowed), with a static test OTP. Paid tiers count as 'memberships' and must be reachable without a real payment.

findings.requirement: Expo localized app display name: set ios.infoPlist.CFBundleAllowMixedLocalizations to true and map locales to JSON files. Each file sets ios.CFBundleDisplayName and android.app_name, and can also translate permission usage descriptions, which are written to InfoPlist.strings during prebuild.
findings.sourceQuote: First, set ios.infoPlist.CFBundleAllowMixedLocalizations: true , then provide a list of file paths to locales .
findings.implicationForProject: Add "locales": {"ar": "./languages/ar.json"} with {"ios": {"CFBundleDisplayName": "غير لي", ...permission strings in Arabic}, "android": {"app_name": "غير لي"}}. This controls the home-screen name only. Store listing names are set separately in App Store Connect and Play Console.

findings.requirement: Expo right-to-left support: the current docs describe SDK 58 and later, where RTL is enabled by default. On iOS the device language must also be one of the app's supported locales, declared with the supportedLocales option. On earlier SDKs, RTL was enabled by default except in Expo Go.
findings.sourceQuote: This section describes the behavior in SDK 58 and later . On previous versions, RTL support was enabled by default, except in Expo Go where it was disabled.
findings.implicationForProject: On SDK 57, verify RTL in a development or EAS build, not in Expo Go. Declare Arabic in supportedLocales so the iOS layout flips, otherwise Arabic store screenshots will not show a genuine right-to-left UI.

unresolved: Apple's screenshot page contradicts itself: the 'Required device sizes' list names only 'iPhone with Dynamic Island (medium display)', but the 'Face ID (large display)' row still says it is required when large Dynamic Island screenshots are missing. Uploading both a 1320x2868 set and a 1206x2622 set is the safe workaround.
Apple counts keywords in bytes (100), but the encoding is not documented. The estimate of about 50 Arabic characters assumes UTF-8 (2 bytes per Arabic letter) and is an inference.
Google Play content rating in Egypt: Egypt does not appear in any listed authority's country list, so IARC Generic presumably applies. Google does not state this explicitly for Egypt.

Apple's properties table marks 'Digital Services Act (DSA) Status' as Required, while the App Information page says it is asked 'in order to distribute apps in the EU'. Not verified whether an Egypt-only app can leave it as non-trader or must still answer.
Not verified which iOS SDK the Expo SDK 57 EAS build images use. This decides whether the April 2027 iPhone Duo screenshot requirement (iOS 27.1 SDK or later) applies to this app's builds.

Whether Apple will require an official Egyptian regulatory clearance link (Guideline 1.4.1) for wound-care guidance or the AI assistant could not be verified. No Egyptian Drug Authority guidance on software as a medical device was checked under this topic.
Apple's app icon (1024x1024 App Store icon) and App Preview video specifications were not fetched in this pass.
The exact final rating the IARC questionnaire produces for health or treatment content cannot be known in advance. It depends on how the questionnaire is answered in Play Console.

research.topic: egypt-health: Egypt-specific healthcare and privacy rules for Dress My Wound / غير لي (status as of 2026-10-14)

findings.requirement: Under Egypt's PDPL (Law 151/2020), health data (psychological, mental, physical or genetic) is SENSITIVE personal data. Children's data is always sensitive.
findings.sourceQuote: Health data (psychological, mental, physical, or genetic).
findings.implicationForProject: Treat all wound photos, wound and condition notes, AI-assistant health conversations, visit records and nurse/doctor clinical notes as sensitive data. Data from patients under 18 is sensitive whatever its type. Classify them in the data inventory and the record of processing.

findings.requirement: The Executive Regulations of the PDPL are Minister of Communications and IT Decree No. 816 of 2025. The PDPC cites 'Executive Regulation No. 816 of 2025'. The Gazette reproduction says it was published in Al-Waqa'i al-Misriya issue 244 (follow-up A) on 1 Nov 2025 and takes effect the day after publication (2 Nov 2025).
findings.sourceQuote: Egyptian Personal Data Protection Law (PDPL) and its Executive Regulation No. 816 of 2025
findings.implicationForProject: The Executive Regulations are issued and in force, so compliance is mandatory now. The decree number is confirmed on the official PDPC site. The publication and effective dates come from a reproduction of the Gazette text (https://alhasswalawfirm.com/law-library/decree-816-2025), not from the Gazette itself.

findings.requirement: PDPL issuance Article 6 says addressees must comply within one year of the date the Executive Regulations are issued. Baker McKenzie (7 Oct 2026) puts the end of the grace period at 31 Oct 2026. CMS reads it as enforcement from 1 Nov 2026.
findings.sourceQuote: This grace period is therefore set to expire on 31 October 2026.
findings.implicationForProject: Any launch from now on falls after or within about two weeks of full enforcement. The company needs its PDPC license or permit, a registered DPO, a consent mechanism and records in place before go-live. Do not plan around a grace period.

findings.requirement: Data users must get a license or permit from the PDPC. A license lasts 3 years and a permit 1 year, both renewable. The types are Controller/Processor, Controller, Processor, E-Marketing (for self or on behalf of others), Cross-Border Data Transfer, and Use of Visual Monitoring Tools.
findings.sourceQuote: The duration of a license is three years (renewable), while the duration of a permit is one year (also renewable).
findings.implicationForProject: The operating company needs a Controller (or Controller/Processor) license that covers sensitive health data. It needs an E-Marketing license if it sends promotional push/SMS/email (for example TetraSol promotions or subscription upsells), and a Cross-Border Transfer license if any backend or AI provider is outside Egypt. Applications go through https://portal.pdpc.gov.eg, which has a licensing questionnaire.

findings.requirement: PDPL Article 12: a controller or processor may not collect, transfer, store, process or give access to sensitive data except under a License from the Center. Outside cases authorized by law, it must get the data subject's explicit written consent. Children's data needs the legal guardian's consent.
findings.sourceQuote: the Controller or the Processor must obtain the explicit written consent of the Data Subject.
findings.implicationForProject: Require a separate, explicit, unbundled consent step for processing health data before onboarding finishes. Do not bury it in the Terms of Service. Patients must be able to withdraw it, and it must be logged. Source is the statute text in a third-party bilingual copy whose English is an unofficial translation.

findings.requirement: Executive Regulations Article 14 (sensitive data) requires: (1) a PDPC license or permit; (2) explicit written consent, on paper or electronically, from the data subject or a child's guardian; (3) the data must be essential to the purpose; (4) the PDPC security standards; (7) secure electronic records of sensitive-data consents and of erasure, correction and stop-processing requests and how they were carried out.
findings.sourceQuote: الحصول على موافقة كتابية صريحة (ورقيا أو الكترونيا )من الشخص المعنى بالبيانات
findings.implicationForProject: Electronic consent is acceptable. Build a tamper-evident consent ledger recording user ID, consent version and text hash, timestamp, locale (Arabic and English) and withdrawal. Keep an audit log of deletion and correction requests and when they were completed. Collect only the health data needed to match patients with providers and deliver care. Source is a law firm's reproduction of the Gazette text.

findings.requirement: Executive Regulations Article 15: for children under 15, the guardian's explicit written consent (paper or electronic), including its time scope, is required before data is collected. For ages 15 to 18, the guardian's consent must also be provided.
findings.sourceQuote: لبيانات الأطفال الأقل من ١٥ سنة الحصول قبل جمع بياناتهم على موافقة كتابية صريحة
findings.implicationForProject: Either limit patient accounts to users 18 and over, or build a guardian/dependent profile flow with guardian e-consent for any patient under 18. Line this up with the app-store age rating.

findings.requirement: Cross-border transfer: personal data may not leave Egypt without a prior cross-border transfer license or permit from the PDPC, plus either an adequacy whitelist or the guarantees in Article 16. Article 15 exceptions, for example medical care or contract performance, still need the data subject's explicit consent. Executive Regulations Article 16 also requires the data subject's consent for transfers.
findings.sourceQuote: Data users are prohibited from transferring personal data outside the Arab Republic of Egypt, unless they have obtained a prior “cross-border data transfer license or permit”
findings.implicationForProject: Hosting in a non-Egyptian cloud region, or sending health data or wound images to a foreign AI or LLM provider, needs a PDPC cross-border license or permit and disclosed consent. Two options: host and process health data in Egypt and keep the AI provider inside the licensed scope, or get the transfer license and collect explicit cross-border consent in the app. Also list processors such as push and analytics services.

findings.requirement: Breach notification: notify the PDPC within 72 hours of becoming aware of a breach, or immediately where national security is involved. Notify affected data subjects within 3 days of notifying the PDPC; the FAQ also says 3 working days elsewhere.
findings.sourceQuote: Notify the PDPC within 72 hours from becoming aware of the breach.
findings.implicationForProject: Write an incident-response runbook with a 72-hour PDPC clock. Keep the DPO's contact details on file and have a template for notifying users in the app or by email in Arabic.

findings.requirement: Data-subject rights cover information, breach notice, access, withdrawal, rectification, erasure, restriction, objection and portability. A recipient must respond within 6 working days of a request.
findings.sourceQuote: The recipient must respond within six working days from the date of submission.
findings.implicationForProject: The privacy center needs self-service export, correction, deletion and consent withdrawal, and a tracked ticket queue with an SLA of 6 working days or less. This sits alongside the app-store account-deletion requirement.

findings.requirement: PDPL Article 8: the legal representative of a juristic-person controller or processor must appoint a competent DPO and register them in the PDPC's DPO record. The PDPC runs DPO certificate and registration services.
findings.sourceQuote: shall appoint within its legal entity and its personnel structure, a competent employee to be responsible for the protection of Personal Data
findings.implicationForProject: Appoint and register a DPO before applying for the license, since Executive Regulations Article 21 requires the DPO contract with the license application. Publish the DPO contact in the privacy notice.

findings.requirement: Penalties: collecting, disclosing, storing or transferring sensitive data without consent or legal authorization (Article 41), and breaching the cross-border rules (Article 42), are each punishable by at least 3 months' imprisonment and/or a fine of EGP 500,000 to 5,000,000.
findings.sourceQuote: a fine not less than five hundred thousand Egyptian Pounds and not exceeding five million Egyptian Pounds
findings.implicationForProject: Gaps in health-data consent and cross-border transfers carry criminal exposure. Treat them as launch blockers.

findings.requirement: The PDPC e-portal launched in October 2026 and takes license, permit and accreditation applications. Creating a profile requires Digital Egypt authentication, which is tied to an Egyptian National ID, so foreign controllers or processors need an authorized local representative.
findings.sourceQuote: creating a profile and submitting applications require authentication through the Egyptian government’s Digital Egypt platform
findings.implicationForProject: If the app's operator or data processor is a non-Egyptian entity, appoint an Egyptian local representative to file the applications. The portal is live at https://portal.pdpc.gov.eg.

findings.requirement: Executive Regulations Article 19 fee table: an annual Controller/Processor license fee for juristic persons, scaled by record count. 1 to 100,000 personal-data records are exempt. A Controller-only or Processor-only license costs half. Permit fees (Article 20) are exempt for 1 to 25,000 records.
findings.sourceQuote: من ١ إلى ١٠٠ ألف معفى من رسوم الترخيص
findings.implicationForProject: At launch scale, the license fee may be zero, but the license is still required. The fee table in this transcription has apparent typos, so confirm the amounts through the PDPC portal.

findings.requirement: PDPC contacts: hotline 17372 and email info@pdpc.gov.eg, taken from the official portal's footer configuration.
findings.sourceQuote: value:"info@pdpc.gov.eg" ... value:"17372"
findings.implicationForProject: The privacy notice can name the PDPC as the supervisory authority users may complain to, with these contact details.

findings.requirement: Egypt emergency numbers: Ambulance 123, Fire 180, Police 122, Tourist police 126. The Health Ministry and the Egyptian Ambulance Organization use 123 as the ambulance hotline; it was disrupted temporarily in 2025, according to news reports.
findings.sourceQuote: Ambulance: 123
findings.implicationForProject: Show a persistent 'Emergency? Call 123 (Ambulance)' action in Arabic and English, using tel:123, on patient screens, the AI assistant, booking and symptom-entry flows. State that the app is not an emergency service. Keep the numbers server-configurable. The source is the UK government (FCDO), an official but foreign source; no Egyptian government page could be fetched to confirm it.

findings.requirement: The ethics code currently posted by the Egyptian Medical Syndicate is Minister of Health Decree 238/2003 of 5 Sep 2003. Its Article 15 forbids a doctor from firmly diagnosing a disease or recommending treatment from oral, written or visual data without examining the patient in person.
findings.sourceQuote: لا يجوز للطبيب الجزم بتشخيص مرض أو التوصية بعلاج من خلال بيانات شفهية أو كتابية أو مرئية دون مناظرة المريض وفحصه شخصيا
findings.implicationForProject: Remote features (chat, photo review, the AI assistant) must not present a definitive diagnosis or prescription. Position them as triage, education, wound-care guidance and booking, and keep diagnosis and treatment within the in-person home visit. The quote is reconstructed from an OCR'd official PDF; the wording matches Youm7's quotation of Article 15.

findings.requirement: In July 2024 the Syndicate proposed amending Article 15 to allow diagnosis, tests and prescribing by remote means, limited to approved platforms and licensed practitioners. No source confirms the General Assembly adopted it. The official site still posts the 2003 text, and the October 2026 General Assembly agenda reported in the news is about media-appearance rules.
findings.sourceQuote: ويحق للطبيب تشخيص المرض وطلب فحوصات ووصف العلاج عن طريق أي وسيلة من وسائل التواصل عن بُعد
findings.implicationForProject: Do not build or market teleconsultation and remote prescribing on the assumption that the amendment is in force. Put any future video-consult feature behind a feature flag.

findings.requirement: The ethics code (Decree 238/2003, as posted by the Syndicate) prohibits doctors from: (a) using intermediaries in practising the profession, paid or unpaid; (b) letting their name be used to promote medicines, treatments or any commercial purpose; (c) requesting or accepting any reward for prescribing specific medicines or devices, or for sending patients to a specific hospital, nursing home, pharmacy or place for tests or for buying medical supplies.
findings.sourceQuote: الاستعانة بالوسطاء في مزاولة المهنة سواء كان ذلك بأجر أو بدون أجر
findings.implicationForProject: The highest-risk area for the TetraSol store: never pay doctors or nurses commissions, bonuses or fee discounts tied to recommending or selling TetraSol products, and do not use clinicians' names or images in TetraSol marketing. The legal model of the matching platform and its fees should be reviewed against the 'intermediaries' prohibition. The quote is reconstructed from an OCR'd official PDF and the article number is not legible.

findings.requirement: Egyptian Medical Syndicate (ems.org.eg) has official online inquiry services: search a doctor by full or partial name to see their specialty, look up licensed hospitals and clinics, and look up the branch syndicate. The physician registration portal is register.ems.org.eg. No public API was found.
findings.sourceQuote: ابحث عن طبيب بالاسم أو جزء منه وتعرف على تخصصه
findings.implicationForProject: Use the Syndicate lookup as one manual credential check for doctors. Also collect and verify the Syndicate membership card or registration certificate, the MOHP practice license and the national ID, and record who verified them and when. Re-verify periodically. Do not claim automated Syndicate verification.

findings.requirement: Law 415/1954 Article 1, as reproduced: practising medicine requires registration in the Ministry of Health's register of doctors and on the Medical Syndicate roll. Law 153/2019 is reported to make registration valid for 5 renewable years.
findings.implicationForProject: Doctor onboarding must collect both the MOHP practice license (with its expiry) and Syndicate registration. Block bookings when the license has expired.

findings.requirement: The Medical Liability and Patient Safety Law (Law 13/2025) was issued on 28 April 2025 and takes effect the day after 6 months from publication. It defines 'medical service' to include consultations and nursing care, requires written informed consent on the Health Ministry's form, and requires practitioners and facilities to join a government medical-error insurance fund within 6 months of the fund statute's issuance.
findings.sourceQuote: يلتزم كل من يزاول إحدى المهن الطبية والمنشآت المبينة بالقانون المرافق بالاشتراك فى الصندوق
findings.implicationForProject: Home visits by doctors and nurses are 'medical services' under this liability regime. Provider terms should require providers to comply with consent and record-keeping rules and to join the insurance fund. The app can support informed-consent capture but must not stand in for the provider's own consent obligation. The effective date is approximate: sources say 28 or 29 Oct 2025.

findings.requirement: The Egyptian Drug Authority's definition of 'medical device' covers 'application software' and any 'material or other article' meant for diagnosis, monitoring, treatment or alleviation of disease or injury. This comes from EDA guideline EDREX:GL.CAMD.003, version 03, effective 01/09/2025. Registration runs through EDA's Central Administration of Medical Devices.
findings.sourceQuote: Medical Device: means any instrument, apparatus, appliance, tool, application software, implant, material or other article
findings.implicationForProject: (1) An AI feature that assesses, grades or monitors wounds for diagnosis or treatment could be software as a medical device needing EDA registration. Keep the AI assistant to general education and wellness, with no diagnostic claims, unless it is registered. (2) TetraSol wound-care products sold in the store are likely medical devices and need valid EDA registration or import approval; show the registration number and do not make unapproved claims. No dedicated EDA guideline for software as a medical device was found.

findings.requirement: No dedicated Egyptian telemedicine or digital-health-platform law or Health Ministry licensing decree was found. Commentary says telemedicine relies on general laws: the E-Signature law (15/2004), the Cybercrime law (175/2018), the PDPL (151/2020) and the Syndicate law (45/1969). Law 51/1981 licenses medical establishments, defined as 'places' (clinics, hospitals and similar), with licenses from the governor; it does not address home-care companies.
findings.sourceQuote: Regulations specific to telemedicine are being developed
findings.implicationForProject: Whether the platform or its home-care operation needs a Health Ministry license is unconfirmed. Get Egyptian regulatory counsel to confirm with the Ministry's free-treatment (العلاج الحر) and licensing departments before launch. Meanwhile, contract only individually licensed practitioners, or licensed home-care establishments, and do not represent the app itself as a healthcare provider.

unresolved: Executive Regulations publication and effective dates (1 and 2 Nov 2025, Al-Waqa'i al-Misriya issue 244) were checked only against non-official reproductions; the Gazette itself was not fetched.
Exact compliance deadline: 31 Oct 2026 (Baker McKenzie) or 1 Nov 2026 (CMS). Whether the PDPC has granted any extension or transitional relief was not found.

The PDPC guideline PDFs (Data Subject Consent, Licenses and Permits v1.1 of 26 Jan 2026, Lawful Bases) could not be downloaded because the portal loads documents dynamically. Requirements such as Arabic-language consent and the 90-working-day license review come only from law-firm summaries.

Health Ministry licensing of home-care, home-nursing or home-visit companies, or of digital booking platforms: no applicable decree found. Law 51/1981 covers fixed 'places' only. Decree 36/2024 on non-governmental health facilities was seen only by title.

Telemedicine: whether the Medical Syndicate General Assembly adopted the 2024 Article 15 amendment, and whether any Health Ministry telehealth guideline exists ('National Telehealth Guidelines 2023' appears only in market-research reports).

Unified emergency number 112: whether it is live nationwide could not be confirmed from an official source; reports are from 2022 plus one state-media mention. No Egyptian government page listing 123, 122 and 180 could be fetched.
Fire and civil-defence number: 180 (UK FCDO and most sources) versus 125 (AUC page).

Nursing Syndicate: official website and any public nurse-registration lookup were not found. The nursing-syndicate law (reportedly Law 115/1976) and the nurse practice-licensing rules were not verified.
Medical Syndicate ethics code: the article number of the intermediaries and commissions provision was not legible in the OCR'd official PDF.
EDA: no specific guidance found on software as a medical device or AI classification, and no confirmation of TetraSol products' EDA registration status.
Whether a doctor-matching platform charging platform fees counts as a prohibited 'intermediary' (الوسطاء) under the ethics code; needs Egyptian legal counsel.

PDPL statute text was read from a third-party bilingual copy with an unofficial English translation (privacylaws.com); the original Gazette version (published around 15 Jul 2020 per secondary sources) was not fetched.

contradictions: Subscription sales channel on Android. apple-health-payments says 'a Silver/Gold/Platinum plan bought via Paymob on Android or web may be honored on iOS'. google-policy says SKUs that are mostly digital, or marketed as digital, must use Play Billing in Egypt: Play Billing is live there, steering is banned, and no alternative-billing program covers Egypt before at least 2027-09-30. Resolution: inside the Android app the tiers must be sold through Play Billing. Paymob for tiers is allowed only on the web. Google lets an app give access to content paid for elsewhere and does not require cross-platform parity (verified, answer/10281818). On iOS, 3.1.3(b) still requires the same tiers to be on sale as IAP.

Where the real-world perks go in a mixed tier. apple-health-payments recommends one IAP subscription that includes the physical perks (priority matching, reduced platform fee). google-policy recommends selling only the digital/AI part through Play Billing and putting the real-world benefits into Paymob-priced visits. Both choices pull against Apple 3.1.3(e) and Play Payments §3, which forbid store billing for physical services. The two findings also classify 'priority matching' differently: google-policy calls it 'arguably digital', and apple-health-payments leaves it unresolved. One cross-store classification is needed, and neither recommendation has official confirmation.

Paying for consultations is not symmetric across stores. Google exempts all regulated clinical services from Play Billing, whether live, remote or asynchronous. Apple exempts only real-time 1:1 services under 3.1.3(d), so asynchronous chat or AI-plus-clinician consults on iOS may need IAP. The google-policy implication ('remote consults can be charged through Paymob') must not be copied into the iOS payment classifier.

Account deletion. apple-privacy says a link straight to a web deletion page is allowed. apple-health-payments says deletion 'must be started in-app'. Google requires both an in-app path and a public web deletion URL. Building both meets all three readings.

16 KB page-size timeline. The blog gave Nov 1, 2025, forum-quoted emails mention May 31, 2026, and the developer page blocks updates from Feb 1, 2027. The Play Console technical page says 'new app bundles uploaded ... must support them'. The finding's implication ('required now') and its 'official-but-ambiguous' rating conflict with the 'verified-official' rating of the Play Console finding.
Inconsistent confidence for the same text. Guideline 5.1.3 (health data, no PHI in iCloud) is rated 'official-but-ambiguous' in apple-privacy and 'verified-official' in apple-health-payments.

Apple's own sources contradict each other in three places. (a) The screenshot page header requires the medium-display Dynamic Island set, while the Face ID card falls back to the large-display set. (b) The iPhone Duo requirement is triggered by the 'iOS 27.1 SDK or later' on the spec page but by 'any apps or games submitted' in the news post. (c) Expo's SDK 54 changelog says predictive back would become the default in SDK 55/56, but the current docs still say 'Default to false'.
weaklySourced: The rule that the 1024x1024 App Store icon must have no alpha channel (ITMS-90717) comes only from Developer Forums and third-party reports. The CI check is still a reasonable safeguard.

That a brand-new Play app (not an update) is blocked at upload today without 16 KB support rests on a community Product Expert and general Play Console wording. The current developer page (updated 2026-09-16) gives no date for new apps.
The 16 KB extension to May 31, 2026 comes only from Play emails quoted in forums.
The date Apple added 'including third-party AI' to 5.1.2(i) (Nov 13, 2025) comes only from secondary sources. The current wording itself is verified.

The mixed digital/physical subscription design (IAP covering the physical perks, or a split plan) rests on a forum thread Apple never answered. It is speculation and must not be presented as Apple-approved.
That 'priority matching' counts as a digital feature is the researcher's inference, not policy text.
That iCloud device backups count as 'storing PHI in iCloud' is an inference. Excluding PHI files from backup is a cautious design choice, not a confirmed rule.
That the Hermes xcframework in RN 0.86.3 ships a valid privacy manifest and signature is unconfirmed (no manifest found in the podspec).
Paymob iOS/Android SDK privacy-manifest coverage and data collection were never checked, yet they feed the nutrition label and the Data safety form.
The Expo SDK 57 predictive-back default conflicts between the changelog and the docs.
Whether uploads are blocked until the Oct 13, 2026 DPLA is accepted is not stated by Apple.
Google's 'Expanded Billing Choice' reaching Rest of World on 2027-09-30 is forward-looking, and fees for that region are 'forthcoming'. Do not plan pricing around it.
The 'Health apps declaration mandatory since 2024-08-31' date has no supporting quote.
That an individual Apple developer account 'is likely to be rejected' is an inference. 5.1.1(ix) says 'should'. Google's Organization-account rule for health apps is the binding one.

The google-policy topic is cut off mid-finding (Photo/Video, then Contacts for API 37). Target audience, Families, the Subscriptions policy and the rest of the Play policy findings cannot be assessed.
missing: Egypt Personal Data Protection Law 151/2020 and its Executive Regulations (Ministerial Decree 816/2025). They require a PDPC controller/processor licence, a separate cross-border-transfer permit (needed for any non-Egyptian AI provider, cloud host or SDK backend), written Arabic consent for sensitive data such as health data, a registered DPO, a record of processing activities (ROPA) with retention periods, and breach notice to the PDPC within 72h. Enforcement begins about 31 Oct to 1 Nov 2026, roughly 17 days away. This is the single biggest gap. Verified.

Google Play AI-Generated Content policy: the AI assistant chatbot needs an in-app 'report/flag' control for offensive AI output that works without leaving the app. Verified. Apple Guideline 1.2 (filtering, report, block and published contact for user-generated content) probably also applies to doctor/patient/nurse messaging. Not verified here.

Egyptian health-advertising Law 206/2017. Promoting health products and services (TetraSol store promotions, store-listing claims, push or email marketing) needs prior approval from the dedicated committee, with penalties including imprisonment and fines of EGP 50k to 100k. The status of its executive regulations is unclear. Verified via a law-firm summary only.

Egyptian Drug Authority registration of TetraSol products (wound dressings and medical devices) sold in the app, and Egyptian limits on selling medicines online (pharmacy law). These also affect Apple 1.4.3 and Google's prescription-drug and unapproved-substance rules. Not verified.

Licensing for clinicians and services: verifying Medical Syndicate and Nursing Syndicate registration, Ministry of Health and Population (MoHP) licensing of home-care and medical establishments, any Egyptian telemedicine rules, and the medical-liability and patient-safety regime. These set who is the 'legal entity providing the services' under Apple 5.1.1(ix). Not verified.

Egyptian Consumer Protection Law 181/2018: Arabic-language terms, e-commerce disclosures, return and refund rights for physical store orders and visit cancellations, and auto-renewal disclosure for web or Paymob plans. Not verified.

Tax and invoicing for Paymob sales: Egyptian Tax Authority e-invoice and e-receipt obligations, VAT on platform fees compared with exempt medical services, commercial registration and tax card for Paymob merchant onboarding. The findings also say nothing on Google Play collecting tax in Egypt (only Apple's is covered). Not verified.

Statutory retention periods for medical records and payments in Egypt. Flagged unresolved in the findings, but they drive the deletion flow, the privacy policy, the Data safety form and the PDPL ROPA.

Subscription lifecycle mechanics: App Store Server Notifications v2, Play Real-Time Developer Notifications (RTDN), acknowledging Play purchases within 3 days (unacknowledged purchases are auto-refunded), server-side receipt validation, grace and hold periods, refund/revocation handling, and merging entitlements across IAP, Play and web Paymob.
Google Play Subscriptions policy (offer transparency, easy cancellation, trial disclosure). It is missing, and the google-policy section is cut off.

Android foreground-service-type and background-location declarations in Play Console if nurses are tracked live or location runs in the background. Also the matching iOS UIBackgroundModes justification.
Paymob, payments and PCI: merchant KYC, PCI DSS scope (aim for hosted checkout, SAQ-A), and Apple Pay via Paymob in Egypt (merchant ID and domain verification) if offered for physical goods.
IAP commission and price points in EGP (Apple Small Business Program, Play 15% subscription rate). Flagged unresolved, with no pricing plan.
Egyptian NTRA or import rules on encryption. Flagged unresolved.
